* DONE [#C] The consent gate is decorative against a live adapter: permission is granted per connection, not per question
:PROPERTIES:
:OBR_SCHEMA_VERSION: 17
:ID:       acat-08l
:LABELS:   []
:ISSUE_TYPE: task
:CREATED:  [2026-08-14 Fri 12:14]
:MODIFIED: [2026-08-14 Fri 12:55]
:CREATED_BY: johnw
:FINISHED: [2026-08-14 Fri 12:55]
:CLOSE_REASON: Fixed in 3b2ab57 and live-verified. Permission is now a function of the question under way (Exec.permissionByCode: .ack grants, every ask denies; Settings.permission overridable; Conn.asked/decisions record each decision with the question that provoked it; Config.permission now only covers requests arriving outside any question, set to .cancel by both harnesses). Plus the empirical counterpart: Artifact.fingerprint/WorkspaceDiff — the workspace is hashed after seeding and at the end, the difference is reported either way, and a run that performed no act (read off the replayed transcript, not the command line) and changed files exits 1 naming them. Negative controls in stub_adapter.py: --write-on-ask (the live defect's shape) must be denied and leave the workspace unchanged; --write-anyway must be caught by the fingerprint. LIVE: refusing run leaves the 323-byte seed byte-identical (md5 unchanged), with two DENIED Bash requests recorded — one of them the author trying to compile its patch in /tmp, OUTSIDE the workspace where the fingerprint is blind, caught only by the permission layer; consenting run grants exactly once during the ack and writes a 1090-byte parser, no strcpy, clean under -Wall -Wextra and ASan/UBSan. RESIDUE (filed separately): denial cost 0 extra turns in this run, contradicting the ~97k-token figure in the docstring, and the harness discards the usage object that would settle it; adapter substituted claude-fable-5 -> opus-4-8 with the narration concatenated onto a reviewer's APPROVE, which decodeVerdict then read as an objection and bought a revision round.
:SOURCE_REPO: agent-cat
:SOURCE_REPO_PATH: /Users/johnw/src/agent-cat
:ORIGINAL_SIZE: 0
:END:

Found by the live run on 2026-08-14 (workflow w5sz6gul7, live stage). SYMPTOM: in the REFUSING run (owner answered no, transcript has six turns and no 'tool apply' line, bill 6) the scratch parse.c was nevertheless replaced with the hardened 823-byte version (seed is 323 bytes, md5 f18314ef... -> 8e856c16...). Timestamps place the write inside the AUTHOR's draft turn (dir birth 12:03:34, file birth 12:04:08, author turn spans ~12:03:49-12:04:23), and it is a birth not a modification: write-and-rename, the signature of an editing tool. CAUSE: Agentic/Core/Acp.lean:271 'permission : Permission := .grant' is a single connection-wide policy that nothing sets; pickAllow answers allow_once to every session/request_permission regardless of the question's Code. To the permission layer, 'ask text model author' and 'act tool apply' are the same thing, so the program's ask/act distinction and the case ok { no -> done } consent branch are unenforceable against a live agent. Harden.no_ack_of_refused still holds — it is about acknowledgements, not bytes — which is exactly the point: there is no theorem and no runtime check saying 'a refused run leaves the workspace as it found it'. FIX (two parts): (1) make the permission decision a function of the QUESTION, not of the connection: grant only for the act (.ack), deny for every ask, and document the known consequence of denial (the turn completes with prose in place of an act, ~97k tokens, no protocol signal); thread the current question through Exec into Acp; log each decision in the transcript. (2) Add the empirical counterpart of the consent theorem: fingerprint the workspace before and after a run, report changes, and fail the run when no act was performed and the workspace changed. Cover both with stub tests. ALSO from the same run, separate issues: the adapter substituted claude-opus-4-8 (not in its advertised catalogue) after claude-fable-5 declined on policy grounds, reporting it only as prose inside the answer — so Conn.configValues is not a complete account of what may answer; and all three reviewers approved a draft that was a policy-refusal banner plus prose plus a fenced diff rather than 'a unified diff only'.

(medium) tui/src/Agentic/Tui/App.hs (redirect line and the 1-9 REDIRECT footer key, near lines 1644 and 1975-1978) and manager/test/service_http.py (about line 4736): the redirect line shows on every live monitor, but the digit keys are bound only in serviceNewMutationKey, and an open person answer editor takes the digits first. While a person question is pending, the monitor lists "1 model controlled@spare", but 1 goes into the answer text. Fix: accept and record the change, or add an end-to-end rejected acknowledgement for at least one PC22 control.
3. (low) tui/src/Agentic/Tui/App.hs (about lines 277-279 and 1143-1147): the comments on stateServiceControlOutcome and on the control-completion branch name only cancel, steer and recovery choice, not the redirect or the rejected-acknowledgement outcome. Fix: update both comments.

6. (low) tui/test/ServiceTests.hs, the render check "shows a rejected-stale redirect without a resend": the no-resend part reads a Presentation that the test builds itself without lane state, so it cannot fail. Only tui-redirect step 4 proves that there is no resend. Fix: build the frame from a lane state after a rejected receipt, or remove the claim from the check name.

Also from the implementer limitations: a 409 unsupported-operation on a send race (the offer disappears between render and send) still declares the command unresolved and offers an explicit exact resend, with no end-to-end check; the live-redirect and controls-routing modes, tui/ci/tui.sh, ALLBUILD and the N=1 journey were not run; the new model tests were not shown failing first.

1. (medium) cli/src/Agentic/Cli.hs near lines 718-719 and 2846: the start body's policyDigest is the SHA-256 of the whole targetPolicy object. For routed v2 targets that object already has its own "policyDigest" field (sha256Fingerprint of the policy without that field, runtime/src/Agentic/Runtime/Catalogue.hs near line 455), which the frontend manifest and catalogue carry. The same name holds two values that never match, so a join of the run log to the manifest by policyDigest fails. policySha256 also duplicates the sha256Fingerprint helper. Fix: rename the start field (for example policySha256), derive it from the existing digest, or state the difference in runtime/BROKER.md.
2. (medium) cli/src/Agentic/Cli.hs near lines 2845 and 2851-2855: the start programSha256 hashes the program after facts, but the frontend preparationProgramHash hashes the static program. The start input digests hash the decoded text after the trailing newline is stripped, not the captured bytes that the frontend hashes. These join keys (design record line 51) can disagree between the manager log and the run log. Fix: hash the same program value and the same input bytes as the frontend, or document that the digests are not comparable.
3. (low) runtime/src/Agentic/Runtime/Machine.hs near lines 153-157 and runtime/BROKER.md near lines 148-153: the record is appended before the durable write. If the durable write then fails, the run log keeps an event record for n with no line in events.ndjson. The comment and BROKER.md describe only the failed-append direction, and the planned reader verb joins records to lines. Fix: state in BROKER.md and the Haddock comment that a failed durable write can leave one trailing event record with no line.
4. (low) runtime/test/FlowTests.hs near lines 365-368: the failure is injected as a codec self-decode refusal, which fails before any byte is written. The I/O failure branch of append (hPut or hFlush, then writerBroken) is not exercised through the sink. Fix: add a case in which the run-log handle fails on write.
5. (low, verification) The new runLogSinkChecks test was not shown failing against the code without the append, and cli/ci/policies.sh (named by runtime/AGENTS.md) was not run under the operator direction of 2026-09-29.

HIGH (4 passes): [DecidableEq] on csum_point is provably vacuous at both carriers; it propagates through idMat/id_comp/pow/retryTrunc/Ctx/conv/pin/gate. Fix: drop the binder from the class axiom, classical idMat, propagate removals. Supersedes acat-6pq.

Findings of the end-of-increment review of actor-flow increment 1 (4496dbe4..d4ec7a6d). The conformance and safety lenses each returned "approve with notes" with no critical or high finding. Source: the section "End-of-increment review" of doc/workflow-manager-handoff.md. The first subtask of Phase B repairs medium findings 1 to 4.

Medium:
1. A cancel whose appended record decodes to a value other than the admitted command is refused with storage-unavailable (manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Commands.hs, recordAdmittedCommand). A cancel is exempt only when its append fails. No check covers a cancel with the lossy codec.
2. The manager log flow/<stream>.ndjson grows across lifetimes and nothing prunes it before Phase G. manager/STORAGE.md does not state the storage-quota limit, the storage-unavailable failure on an oversized or undecodable log, or the recovery procedure.
3. manager/STORAGE.md says that no local path enters a body. The review body holds the exact binding bytes, which name the frontend invocation path, the run-root identity and the target arguments.
4. A control delivered before activation of a store-backed run does not pass through flowBroker, so the run log has no control record. runtime/BROKER.md states this limit, but it differs from Delta 1a of the design record.
5. The ext-pi checks and the ext-pi part of gate 5 have no result (also in acat-62j0).

Low:
6. A failed failure-reply append after a rollback leaves no gap entry.
7. A review record that a later pre-commit step rolls back has no ending.
8. Offline credential administration writes no manager-log record.
9. An engine ask without a scope is refused by flowBroker, and no test shows that a store-backed path cannot reach it.
10. A receipt or relay whose decoded value differs from the ledger is carried as the ledger value with no gap entry.
11. The reader loads the whole log prefix before it checks the line bound, and --follow accepts only one run log.
12. Run-log bodies and the output of the verb are not redacted, and runtime/BROKER.md does not say so.
13. A failed append of an ACP permission report fails the turn after the grant was sent.
14. The pending slot of a command record is set after the append, so a deadline in that window leaves the record uncertain.

On a 412 stale-revision refusal, handleServiceSent records only LineageRefused, so every fork edit is lost. The TUI's own automatic result retrieval changes the lineage collection ETag, so a menu opened on the live monitor right after the run succeeds can meet this 412. The evidence is PC/PC28/impl-r1/history-try2.log: 'Lineage fork: refused (412 stale-revision)'. Fix: on a 412, keep the menu and its edits, read the lineage collection again and rebind the observation, or defer opening the menu until a due retrieval settles. Adopted from the 2026-08-14 web survey (comparison judge, acat-k28 phase C). (1) Add a second fold over the existing finite cost tree computing the selective-functors Over/Under pair: the UNDER set is the questions asked in every world (the floor — exactly the panel dispatchable immediately); the OVER set is every question any world can ask (the ceiling). No former, no shape change; sources: Mokhov et al Selective Applicative Functors (static.tex in github.com/snowleopard/selective), Haxl/ApplicativeDo as the cautionary tale (never recover the rung by a heuristic desugarer — GHC's own manual admits ApplicativeDo 'might miss an opportunity'; ours is syntax, {$x} vs {x}). (2) Presentation modeled on Snakemake --dry-run job tables + a --why column naming the binding that forced each question (Snakemake -r). (3) A machine-readable validate mode shaped like AWS ValidateStateMachineDefinition: result OK|FAIL plus diagnostics {code, message, severity, location}, pitched for CI/pre-commit, with the stated stability discipline (rely on result, not on message wording). (4) LlamaIndex framing for docs: the same declarations serve two moments — before a run (every possible path) and after (what happened); our cost tree IS the picture and a transcript is a sub-tree of it.

1. (medium) emacs/wf-service.el lines 2302 to 2323 and 1397 to 1400. RET on a legacy observer row of the service history calls wf-service-open-view, which watches every view resource of the run. Neither the live step nor the offline test opens a legacy row: the live step opens a managed run, and the offline test opens only run_21. If a legacy entry answers 404 for a watched resource, the open can fail or show an empty view. Fix: add an offline test, and if cheap a live substep, that opens a legacy observer row and requires a rendered read-only view. Fix the watch behavior for legacy runs if the test shows a problem.

2. (low) emacs/wf-service.el lines 2160 to 2165. A second save to an existing file reads the outputs and downloads the artifact again before the exclusive write refuses. The refusal is correct and the file stays unchanged, but the refusal costs a full download. Fix: optionally check the target before the download, and keep the excl write as the authoritative refusal.

3. (low) manager/test/service_http.py lines 11432 to 11437. Check 24 proves that no read named the run only from Emacs-side advice on wf-manager-get and wf-manager-download (emacs/wf-manager-live.el line 1608). The harness does not confirm it from the manager log, and it does not assert that the new binding is the third credential. Fix: optionally assert from the manager log that no request named the run after the switch, and record the bound credential in the report.

4. (low) emacs/wf-manager-tests.el line 3398. (should (equal (call-interactively #'wf-result) nil)) checks the constant nil that the wf.el service wrapper returns. Fix: drop the equal check, or assert on the returned file name of wf-service--result directly.

5. (low) emacs/wf-service.el line 2268. Every wf-history and every H creates a new buffer with generate-new-buffer, so repeated use stacks *wf service history*<n> buffers. The README documents a new buffer. Fix: reuse one history buffer per endpoint identity, or document the stacking as intended.

6. (low) README.md line 849. The text "read the local stores as before" describes a change instead of the current state. Fix: state the current state, for example "In local mode, wf-history and the observer read the local stores."

7. (low) emacs/wf-service.el wf-service--result-run. Outside a run view, wf-result offers only the runs of open views and overview members. It does not offer the history row at point. Fix: optionally use the history row at point as the run of wf-result in a service history buffer.

Implementer limitations recorded with PD23: wf-service-save-exact creates the file with O_EXCL and mode 0600 but does not use the private-file-plus-hard-link publication of ext-pi saveExact, so a write failure after creation can leave a partial file (deferred as a security-only item, per the 2026-09-30 direction); opening a legacy observer entry from the history is not exercised live; the service run view key text is now two lines.

1. (medium) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Admission.hs:605-619 (discardAndClose), called from finishEntry at :575: if the discard frame decoded from the relay fails the exact check in sendWorkerDiscard (lossy codec or corrupted append), the send raises WorkerConfiguration. discardAndClose rethrows it before closeWorker, and the exception leaves finishEntry before entryCleanupConfirmed and finalizeKnown. No test covers it, because the lossy fixture changes only cancel frames. Fix: run closeWorker in a finally, define how finalization proceeds when the relayed discard is refused, and add a flow-relay case with a lossy discard frame.

2. (medium) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Admission.hs:938: the requirement says to encode the start frame after reserveDispatch commits. The code runs encodeWorkerStart before reserveDispatch (line 939). An encode failure (WorkerClosed or WorkerConfiguration) now leaves deliverStartNow before the reservation, and the approve stays accepted with no refusal and no attempt recorded. Fix: record the reordering in the design record, or move the encode step after the reservation and refuse with refuseUnrelayed when the encode fails.

3. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Admission.hs:636-643 (relayFrame): for the Refusing start and control relays, a decode or identity mismatch after a successful append returns Left. The command is refused, but the appended relay stays in the manager log with no notice that it was never sent. Fix: append a notice for a relay that was appended but not sent, or document that such a relay was not delivered.

4. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Admission.hs:1045, 942, 1051: an exception after reserveDispatch leaves the ticket reserved, with neither recordRefusal nor discardControlPayload (for example reservedPayload returning Nothing, which throws OwnershipUnavailable, or relayFrame throwing instead of returning Left). Fix: wrap the relay step so that any exception after the reservation goes through refuseUnrelayed.

5. (low) manager/test/AdmissionCheck.hs:1493ff (flowRelayChecks): no test covers a failed non-cancel control relay refused by refuseUnrelayed (Admission.hs:1054), a failed discard relay append that leaves a gap entry (Following and Reserved), or a relayed control rejected by the controlId or re-encode check. The "no live worker" item after a failed start relay checks only that no run log exists (line 1548), not that the worker process exited. Fix: add flow-relay cases for these branches and assert that the refused-start worker process has exited.

6. (low) F12-flow-relay.log: flow-relay prints the fault lines "WorkerUnexpectedExit erased=command StorageUnavailable" after the cancelled run and "WorkerClosed" after the refused start. No run compares them with the behavior before this change. The journey relay order is checked only by the private script journey_relays.py, not by the repository journey. Fix: compare these fault lines with a cancel of a scripted run at HEAD, and consider moving the relay-order assertion into the repository journey check.

Actor-flow increment 1, delta 1b (at most 8 engineering days). Add the manager log, one per Store stream identity, in the private root outside SQLite. It has a leaf lock, synchronized appends, gap notices and a ceiling equal to the mutation-ledger ceiling with the cancel reserve. It records each command after the Store admits it and before COMMIT, plus receipts, reviews with their private binding, relays to workers, requests that end without a run, lifetimes and administration changes. A command whose record cannot be written is refused with storage-unavailable, except a cancel. At the ceiling, ordinary commands are refused with storage-quota (operator decision). Extend the reader to the manager log and its joins. Gate: the unchanged Phase A tui-journey at N1 and then N8, with the reader showing and verifying the whole consent chain and every user step, and a negative control for each check (section 6.1 of the design record). Increment 1 is accepted only as a whole. Design record: proposals/actor-flow-architecture-v2.md (revision 4) in the private resume-20260923 evidence directory. Governing amendment: the "Operator amendment of 2026-09-26: actor flow" section of GOAL.md there.

Non-blocking findings of fess audit fess/pe-PE11-r1.md (2026-10-01) on subtask PE11 (WM-036 shared-vector consumer, part 1: lossless JSON and SSE events in ext-pi/src/manager).

1. (low) decodeEventBlock and decodeRouteBlock in ext-pi/src/manager/events.ts (near 551-553) parse block data with JSON.parse through tryParseJson. It keeps the last duplicate member and has no 64-level depth limit, while Haskell blockData uses decodeStrictValue (manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Protocol/Json.hs near 37-62), which refuses both. No vector covers this. It is documented in ext-pi/README.md and deferred to the security stage under the 2026-09-30 functionality-first direction. Fix: add duplicate-member and depth refusal for SSE block data (for example a small token checker before JSON.parse), together with a vector.
2. (low) The PE11 task text asks for "CR line ends", but the parser refuses a lone carriage return (ext-pi/src/manager/events.ts near 171-172). The code is correct: it matches Events.hs lineOf and the vector "lone carriage return refuses". Fix: correct the WM-036 consumer task wording to "LF and CRLF line ends, a lone CR refuses". No code change.
3. (low) integerOf in ext-pi/test/manager-vectors.test.ts (near 66-71) throws on a non-integral status or repeat count, while ClientCheck.hs rounds these values. The test is only stricter, and no current vector is affected. Optional fix: note the stricter reading in a test comment.

At +RTS -N8, two simultaneous identical deep asks once shared only a single candidate attempt, so one could observe the primary gap while the other continued to the broad fallback. The memo reservation now encloses the entire fallback walk: equal concurrent occurrences share its final success or final failure. The applicative concurrent regression remains intact and passed 100/100 at -N8.

Follow-up from the F9 fess audit of the manager log writer, the manager codecs and the lifetime and shutdown notices (actor-flow delta 1b). None of these findings blocks. Source: fess audit /Users/johnw/Products/agent-cat-workflow-manager/implementation.9tGzKH/service-tui.purvEwEv/resume-20260923/fess/flow-F9-r2.md.

1. (medium) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Flow.hs:195-202 and manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Store.hs:333-334, 467-468: the operator gets no diagnostic when the manager log cannot be opened (for example a log larger than the ceiling, or an owner or permission refusal from PrivateRoot). openManagerFlow keeps the reason only as a Left value, and the results of appendLifetime and appendShutdown are discarded. When the append points are connected, every ordinary command would be refused with storage-unavailable and no visible cause. Fix: report the open failure and each lifetime and shutdown append result on the manager diagnostic channel, or fail the serving open when the log cannot be opened.

Follow-up from the F13 fess audit of the command notices, review endings and request endings (actor-flow delta 1b). None of these findings blocks. Source: fess audit /Users/johnw/Products/agent-cat-workflow-manager/implementation.9tGzKH/service-tui.purvEwEv/resume-20260923/fess/flow-F13-r1.md.

1. (medium) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Store.hs:1292-1296 (runWithAdmission, post-COMMIT appendQueued) and the new STORAGE.md paragraph: the queued notices are appended after COMMIT under mask, not uninterruptibleMask. The append takes an MVar and does file I/O, and the synchronous path rethrows async exceptions. An async exception there (a cancel, a race loser or a timeout) makes runWithAdmission throw for a committed transaction. In attemptTicket the state then reads dispatch-attempted but the action never runs. The documentation says a failed notice cannot make the committed transaction uncertain, which is true only for synchronous failures. Fix: flush the queue under uninterruptibleMask_ with bounded writer I/O, or catch async exceptions during the flush, record gap entries and return the committed value. Otherwise correct the documented guarantee.

2. (medium) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Commands.hs:271 and :391, Admission.hs:797: notices taken with takePostCommit (for example RequestEnded withdrawn or ReviewEnded) are appended in recordReceipt, outside the transaction. If the thread is interrupted between COMMIT and appendPostCommit, they are lost with no gap entry. reconcileCommandAttemptWithAdmission restores only a command notice (Commands.hs:462). Fix: record a gap entry for taken notices that are never appended (a bracket or finally in recordReceipt), or have reconciliation re-derive the endings.

3. (medium) manager/test/AdmissionCheck.hs:1587-1606, manager/test/CommandCheck.hs:1675: no behavioral test asserts a ReviewEnded record (address Approvers profile, reason, position). The causes review-expired, preparation-failed and invalidated, and the edit path, are not tested. Fix: add flow-relay assertions for the review-ended record of the prepared withdraw, and one scenario each for the expired and preparation-failed causes.

4. (medium) manager/test/AdmissionCheck.hs:1587-1590, manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Admission.hs:711-725 and :1137, Application.hs:160: /v1 discard is refused as unsupported-operation before admission, so the discard acceptance item is met by withdrawing a prepared request. A user's withdraw command is then followed by request-ended cause=discarded, while the command's effect says withdrawn. The design lists withdrawn as the cause for a withdraw. Fix: get an operator decision on whether a prepared withdraw names withdrawn or discarded, then adjust the noticeRequestEnding priority and ADMISSION.md.

5. (low) manager/ADMISSION.md (Manager log endings), Store open reconciliation: the restart reconciliation refuses requests and invalidates preparations but appends no per-item request or review ending. The lifetime notice counts them. An edit that returns a queued request to draft also appends no ending. Fix: append a per-item ending, or a gap notice that names each item, at Store open.

6. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Admission.hs:693, AdmissionCheck.hs:1595: the request ending of a refused approval carries aboutCommand=Nothing and does not join the refused approve command. Fix: pass the refused approve's command id into noticeRequestEnding when the cause is refused.

7. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Admission.hs:715: the refused-cause query counts refused approves over every preparation of the reservation, while the reasons query at :716 filters on process_generation. A refused approve from an earlier generation could mislabel a later ending. Fix: filter the refused query on p.process_generation=?, or confirm that reservations never span generations.

8. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Commands.hs:731 and :462: a command notice goes out on any receipt change, even when the state stays the same, and reconciliation can repeat a logged state. The journey shows acknowledged twice. Fix: emit a notice only when receiptState or receiptRefusal changes, or document that notices may repeat a state.

9. (low) manager/test/AdmissionCheck.hs:1602-1606: the assertion that command notices of the approval follow its start relay passes if any CommandChanged follows the relay, whatever its state. Only the private journey_notices.py checks the journey order. Fix: assert the specific dispatch-attempted state and position, and consider moving the journey-order check into the repository.

Non-blocking findings of fess audit fess/pd-PD17-r2.md (2026-10-02) on subtask PD17 (WM-030 part 10, agent-workflows emacs-native endpoint switch and session close, agent-cat manager/test/service_http.py mode emacs-client).

1. (medium) emacs/wf-manager-live.el:707-715. The live close step runs after the revoke step, which waits until the follow loop has ended with refused. When wf-manager-session-close runs live, no poll timer and no request is pending, so the live run never shows close cancelling an active poll or a pending GET against the real manager. Only the offline test wf-manager-session-close-ends-switch covers that. Fix: close a session whose follow loop is still active (close before the revocation, or start and close a short second session after it) and assert that no process or timer remains.

2. (low) emacs/wf-manager.el:3790-3792. The error clause of wf-manager--send turns any signal whose condition is exactly error, raised anywhere inside url-retrieve or wf-manager--retrieve, into (wf-manager-transport-unavailable "connection" ...). An unrelated plain error from url.el would be reported as a connection failure. Fix: also match the message text (Certificate validation failed, Could not create connection) and signal other plain errors again, or keep the clause and its comment.

3. (low) emacs/wf-manager.el:3744. The exchange is pushed onto wf-manager-transport-exchanges before the condition-case, so the re-signal path leaves it in the list with no timer and no callback. Fix: remove the exchange from the transport list before signalling again.

4. (low) manager/test/service_http.py:530,586. Two fragment lines remain in the emacs-client comment block ("# requests and the command receipts after the start" and "# 200. A delayed read of"). Fix: reflow those two paragraphs.

5. (low) emacs/wf-manager.el:3369,3387,4219,4314. New commentary and docstring lines run past the fill column (87, 96, 115 and 88 columns). Fix: refill those paragraphs.

6. (low, accepted limitations) The live delayed-GET step holds a read that has already completed, through advice on wf-manager--session-complete, rather than delaying a real network GET. The kill-buffer check cannot fail, because the client has no kill-buffer hook. The unreachable-port bind-and-release race in the harness remains. The synchronous connect blocks Emacs until the system connect timeout, as the README states. A later item can add a non-blocking TLS open.

7. (low, integrator note) emacs/wf-manager-tests.el embeds a throwaway EC private key and its self-signed certificate for 127.0.0.1 (wf-manager-tests--other-key, wf-manager-tests--other-certificate) for the CA-mismatch test. The key protects nothing and no fixture trusts it, but a secret scanner can flag it on a later push. Fix: generate the key and certificate at test time with python3 or openssl from PATH, and remove the constants.

Non-blocking findings of the fess audit of Phase C subtask PC3 (WM-042 release-quarantine and new runs after a manager crash with one reservation). Report: fess/pc-PC3-r1.md in the private resume-20260923 evidence directory.

1. (medium, pre-existing) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Store.hs (about line 402) and manager/test/service_http.py (failures-manager case 9, third-lifetime reconciliation assert). The restart rule makes every dispatch-attempted command with a start intent unresolved, including the approve of a run that already succeeded. The new third lifetime is the first to observe this, and the test now asserts commands 1 with a comment. Fix: a restart does not reclassify an approve whose run has a terminal observation. Then change the case 9 expectation back to commands 0.
2. (low) manager/test/service_http.py (failures-manager, removed old case 7). The old mode checked that a request waits with profile-busy behind the resource keys of a quarantined reservation. With one profile and one slot, capacity now masks that path. Fix: confirm that another suite covers profile-busy behind a quarantine, or add a fixture-row check in CommandCheck or the admission check.
3. (low) manager/test/credential_cli.py (about lines 70-74 and 156-158) and manager/test/CommandCheck.hs quarantineChecks. A successful offline release has only unit coverage through administerLocally StoreStopped. Fix: add one end-to-end offline release through agentic-run --manager admin on a stopped Store that holds a quarantine, then serve and confirm that the slot is free.
4. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Quarantine.hs (about lines 210-244). The release does not enforce the expiresAt that check-quarantine returns. Evidence from the same lifetime that is older than 600 seconds is accepted while the facts are unchanged. Fix: decide whether the release enforces expiresAt, and document the decision in manager/COMMANDS.md.
5. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Quarantine.hs (about lines 161-170, called at 216). For a launched claim, the release reads the run log while it holds the file slot and the configuration guard, so a concurrent admission poll waits until the release ends. Fix: keep it and its documentation, or read the terminal record before the configuration guard and recheck the digest inside it.
6. (low, cosmetic) manager/COMMANDS.md (administration log paragraph), manager/README.md (worker authority paragraph), manager/STORAGE.md and runtime/BROKER.md. The edited paragraphs were not reflowed and leave over-long lines. Fix: reflow them.

Further limitations recorded by the implementer: only N8 was run; the cleanup-required path and an unreadable run store still have no fixture; the release gives the lost request a new revision (request.changed), so a client that holds an older ETag of that request gets a precondition failure.

Stage M1 of the manager broker amendment decided on 2026-09-25. Add Agentic.Manager.Broker with an injected ManagerBroker (brokerToWorker, brokerFromWorker) and the default directBroker, which applies the original private-pipe operations unchanged. The Worker enforces that the delivered bytes equal the original frame and that each lent operation runs once, on the calling thread, before the broker call returns, so a broker can carry, delay or fail a frame but cannot alter, repeat, reorder or replay one. Thread the broker to a new serveManagerWith. Add manager/BROKER.md, a placement sentence in manager/WORKERS.md and a cross-reference in runtime/BROKER.md. Tests: a counting broker proves every worker frame passes through the seam, a withholding broker proves delivery depends on it, and delivery-check and cancellation negatives cover the Worker check. Place after the first TUI workflow milestone (Phase A) is accepted and before WM-028. Revalidate the worker, admission, approval, control, ingestion and vertical owners at N1 and then N8, with fess and independent review.

1. (medium) emacs/wf-service.el lines 1990 to 2010. No test sends choose-recovery (abandon and failover:N) through wf-control. That path reads the decision again for its ETag, posts the choice to /v1/decisions/{id} and reconciles through wf-manager-recovery-reconciliation. Only the offline listing test covers it, and that test checks neither the body, the If-Match header nor the reconciliation. Fix: add an offline ERT test that chooses failover:1 and abandon through wf-control and asserts the POST target, the decision ETag as If-Match, the exact body {operation, occurrenceId, generation, choice} and one reconciliation read on an uncertain send.

2. (low) manager/test/service_http.py line 10772. Harness step 5 only checks that ifMatch starts with a quote, but PASS 5 and the header comment state that the controls ETag was the If-Match value. The offline tests check that equality for cancel and steer only. Fix: record the controls ETag of each listing read in the report and assert that ifMatch equals it.

3. (low) emacs/wf-service.el lines 1825 and 2012. wf-service--read-optional returns nil on any failed read or decode error. A transport failure on the head-decision read removes every recovery choice without a message, and a failed snapshot read shows "place not published". Fix: treat only the expected 404 of a decision that is no longer pending as absent, and report any other read failure to the user.

4. (low) emacs/wf-service.el lines 1979 to 1989. Only the uncertain steer reconciliation is tested. The uncertain retry (wf-manager-control-passed) and uncertain cancel paths are not tested. Fix: add an offline test that drops the retry POST and checks that one controls read reconciles it with no resend.

5. (low) emacs/wf-manager-live.el line 1297. The emacs-client views step now always waits 61 seconds after the pages step, to stay under the manager limit of 30 ordinary mutations per minute per client. The change is test-only and documented and does not alter the limit, but it adds one minute to every run. Fix: keep it, or replace it with a wait on a 429 Retry-After, and record the trade-off.

6. (low) manager/test/service_http.py lines 5770 and 6193. The tui-controls mode was not run after answer_until_recovery moved into ControlHarness.until_recovery. The tuple arity matches mixed_client by reading, and the method passed in emacs-client-controls. Fix: run the tui-controls mode once at the next integration checkpoint.

Implementer limitations recorded with PD22: choose-recovery through wf-control has offline listing coverage only, the live check covers steer, redirect, retry and cancel; the views step pacing works around the fixed limit of 30 ordinary mutations per minute per client in Agentic.Manager.Client, and no limit was changed; the tui-controls mode was not run. Capability matrix at baseline:
- Trusted catalogue, v1/v2/v3 descriptors, source-aware /wf parsing: present. Downstream wf registry reads 74 rows, but active global configuration names agentic-run. Test candidate will use isolated runner configuration.
- Multi-input form, field-file content loading, draft retention across native views: absent. Current inputs loop through individual editor prompts.

Non-blocking audit findings from B9 (WM-024 protected HTTP boundary, fess report resume-20260923/fess/b1-B9-r1.md).

1. (medium, needs operator authorization) The plaintext refusal is malformed HTTP. A string-gap defect in warp-tls 3.4.14 DenyInsecure output writes twelve spaces, a backslash and the letter r before the line feed on three header lines. service_http.py PLAINTEXT_REFUSAL pins these bytes and doc/api/README.md states them. The security property holds: the refusal carries no resource state and no bearer path. Correcting the bytes needs a warp-tls dependency patch, which only the operator can authorize. If the patch lands, update PLAINTEXT_REFUSAL and the README paragraph.
2. (low) service_http.py boundary TLS 1.2 check passes on any ssl.SSLError. It captures failure.reason but never asserts it, so a certificate or hostname failure would also pass. Assert that the reason contains PROTOCOL_VERSION or WRONG_VERSION.
3. (low) doc/api/README.md refusal table gives 413 size-limit for header fields above 16384 bytes. Warp setMaxTotalHeaderLength 16384 refuses such a header block with 400 before the application runs, so the byte clause in Transport.hs cannot be reached. Remove the byte clause from the 413 row, or state that the HTTP server refuses such headers first with 400.
4. (low) If a client sends no body byte at all, the 15-second Warp connection timeout and the 15-second JSON read bound end at the same moment, so the client gets either 400 malformed-request or a closed connection. The documentation states this, but no test covers it. Accept as documented, or make the body read bound shorter than the Warp timeout so the 400 always arrives first.

The run is never retrieved again, even after its snapshot becomes Verified. Store no result, or a retryable pending marker, for that outcome, and keep a permanent record only for declared refusals.

2. (medium) Accepted adaptation to record: the manager records result verification lazily, when the run outputs are read. For a succeeded run whose snapshot shows referenced, retrieveResult reads the outputs, re-reads the snapshot, and downloads only when that fresh snapshot shows Verified for the same result reference (tui/src/Agentic/Tui/Service.hs near 600-677). No bytes are downloaded without Verified. Record the lazy verification as a contract fact in the manager documentation, or change the manager to verify eagerly.

3. (low) The shared press helper in manager/test/service_http.py (near 709-712) now accepts "did not start: a command is in progress" as a reason to press again, also for the answer key. Accept it only for the retry press, or document why the answer press needs it.

4. (low) saveExact (tui/src/Agentic/Tui/Save.hs near 42-43) returns Left when createLink succeeds and the removal of the private file then fails, although the destination is published. It also needs hard-link support in the destination file system. Treat a failed removal after publication as success with a leftover temporary file, and document the hard-link requirement.

5. (low) Local-mode saveResultFile moved from an O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW open to saveExact (tui/src/Agentic/Tui/App.hs near 1640-1644). The Integrator accepted this as consolidation. Confirm that local-mode behavior and its documentation stay correct.

6. (low) The retry attempt in the receipt address comes from the highest attempt that the TUI snapshot publishes (tui/src/Agentic/Tui/Service.hs near 1051), while the manager builds the address from its own snapshot (manager/src/Agentic/Manager/State.hs near 661). A mismatch leaves the retry uncertain but never completes it falsely. Add a journey assertion that the TUI shows "retry effect observed".

7. (low) A check label in tui/test/ServiceTests.hs (near 1092) says that an unavailable verification downloads nothing, but the check asserts only the referenced case. Rename the check or add the assertion.

8. (low) App.hs imports the new project module Agentic.Tui.Save. The rule says that new code imports only Agentic.Runtime and Agentic.Manager.Client among project modules. Save.hs imports no project module and source-boundaries passed. Confirm that intra-TUI imports of new modules are within the intent of the rule.

Owner directive (2026-08-15): find out whether ACP can talk to running, live sessions; if it can, add that infrastructure to agent-cat, so a workflow run can be observed interactively (the motivating case: an agent-deck session named agent-cat hosting the owner's interactive Claude, watching example/harden.wf run).

Facts already established from our side: agent-cat's ACP client speaks session/new only (Acp.newSession; no session/load anywhere); Adapter.ofName knows stub/claude/codex; --adapter-arg passes argv through verbatim; person questions already reach the operator's keyboard on live runs (Exec.Settings.askPersonOnStdin := !stubbed). A Claude session is owned by one process, so 'attach to the pane's session' may be impossible regardless of protocol support — the research must distinguish resume-into-new-process (fork?) from true live attach.

Research running (workflow wf_709221dd-563): (1) ACP spec semantics of session/load + loadSession capability + any non-stdio transport that reaches an already-running agent + multi-client/observer modes; (2) claude-agent-acp 0.66.0's loadSession behavior and resume/fork semantics under contention; (3) Claude Code/SDK resume semantics and any supported live-attach path.

Scope once research lands: at minimum, client-side session/load (capability-gated), a --session <id> flag on agent-cat run, and honest diagnoses for what cannot be attached; more if the protocol offers more.

Three layers, all confirmed:\n\n1. PROTOCOL. `session/load` is sequential handoff — the agent (a subprocess this client spawned) restores context and MUST replay the whole history as session/update notifications, then the client continues \"as if the session was never interrupted\". stdio-subprocess is the only defined transport (\"The client launches the agent as a subprocess\"; Streamable HTTP is a draft RFD). 1:1 client:session by assumption. The exact missing thing has an open RFD — \"Multi-Client Session Attach\" (PR #533, proposal stage since 2026-02: \"There is no mechanism for a second client to 'attach' to a live, in-progress session\"). Correction recorded: ACP versions are integers (current stable 1, which Acp.lean already sends); \"2025-11-25\" is our MCP revision, not ACP.\n\n2. * DONE [#C] Engine: agent-deck as a payload transport beside the ACP adapters — send/output into live sessions
:PROPERTIES:
:OBR_SCHEMA_VERSION: 17
:ID:       acat-agent-deck-engine-vv6
:LABELS:   []
:ISSUE_TYPE: feature
:CREATED:  [2026-08-15 Sat 22:16]
:MODIFIED: [2026-08-17 Mon 19:52]
:CREATED_BY: johnw

:SOURCE_REPO: agent-cat
:SOURCE_REPO_PATH: /Users/johnw/src/agent-cat
:ORIGINAL_SIZE: 0
:END:

Owner directive (2026-08-15): add agent-deck as another ENGINE for delivering and working with payloads, alongside claude and codex — and able to talk to claude and codex via agent-deck.

Why this matters beyond parity: it is the answer to the live-session question acat-acp-live-session-99n closed negatively. ACP cannot reach a live session at any layer; agent-deck can — `agent-deck session send <id> <message>` delivers into any running pane (Claude, Codex, Pi, OpenCode) and `session output` polls the last response, sidestepping the single-writer rollout hazard entirely. A deck engine therefore gives `agent-cat run` the interactive-observation mode the owner originally asked for: the workflow's questions land in a live, watched pane, and answers come back from it.

Scope sketch (agent-cat side):
- A new engine beside the ACP adapters, with a different transport: not stdio ACP but the agent-deck CLI — send a rendered prompt via `agent-deck session send`, poll `session output` for the reply, decode with the existing per-kind Decode. Turn boundaries and timeouts need design (deck output is text, not structured stop reasons); `session approve` maps to the permission axis for codex targets.
- CLI surface: something like `agent-cat run program.wf --engine deck --session <deck-session>`; person questions can stay on the operator's stdin, or be routed into the same pane — design choice.
- The primitives to build on, verified in the owner's probe notes: send, output, approve, fork, handoff, parent/child links, -assert-done sentinels, transition notifications, codex-hooks/gemini-hooks.
- Safety rules to encode, from the owner's architecture note: never ACP-loadSession a thread whose TUI is live (single writer per rollout) — the deck's send is the safe path to a live session; one writer per worktree.
- Relation to the three-planes doctrine (repo = data plane, deck = control plane, ACP = embedding layer for headless/IDE): the deck engine is agent-cat's control-plane citizenship; the ACP adapters remain the headless path, and the parked --session/loadSession feature (99n) remains the headless-handoff path.

The owner's full architecture note is preserved below for the design round.
---
[Three planes: 1. repository as data plane (AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md symlink, .agents/skills, obr/PLAN.org as vendor-neutral ledger; doctrine: work is handed off via issues and commits, chat channels only signal). 2. agent-deck as control plane (session send/output/approve/fork/handoff, parent-child links, -assert-done, transition notifications, codex-hooks/gemini-hooks; launch through agent-deck launch; name decks after lanes; use send/output/handoff as the inter-vendor mailbox instead of raw ACP). 3. ACP adapters as embedding layer (IDE hosting and headless programmatic control; Claude-hosted ACP sessions appear in Claude's peer registry, codex's do not; Claude↔Claude native, Claude↔codex via deck (live) or ACP session/new-loadSession (headless); never loadSession a live codex thread. Roles: Claude Code orchestrator/reviewer; Codex heads-down implementer in isolated worktree; Pi third opinion; one writer per worktree; checkpoint self-sync (obr sync --import-only + deck messages + labels) in AGENTS.md; Nix hygiene: pin adapter+CLI pairs together via CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE/CODEX_PATH.]

(medium) runtime/src/Agentic/Runtime/Flow.hs (statesUncertain), runtime/test/FlowReaderTests.hs, doc/agent-cat.texi and runtime/BROKER.md: statesUncertain holds every open ask of an ended log, including a log that has its stop. Follow-up from the F10 fess audit of the command, receipt and failure records in the admission transaction (actor-flow delta 1b). None of these findings blocks. Source: fess audit /Users/johnw/Products/agent-cat-workflow-manager/implementation.9tGzKH/service-tui.purvEwEv/resume-20260923/fess/flow-F10-r1.md.

1. (medium) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Store.hs:1247: the rollback failure reply reuses the command's class from PendingCommand, which is Refusing for every ordinary command. appendManager keeps no gap entry for a failed Refusing append, and the result is discarded. If that append fails, a definitely refused command has no reply and reads as uncertain. Fix: append the failure reply as Following (Reserved for a cancel) and do not discard the result.

2. (medium) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Commands.hs:383-386: after COMMIT, if the appended receipt decodes to a value that differs from the ledger receipt, the response carries the ledger receipt with no gap entry or notice. Fix: keep a gap entry or notice for the mismatch, and test it with a lossy receipt codec.

3. (medium) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Commands.hs:347-353: no check exercises the capture branch of admittedCommandBody (command_captures row, Drafts.hs:435). A fault there would refuse every production capture with storage-unavailable. Fix: add a flow-mode capture command to flowCommandChecks that asserts the CaptureReference in the command record.

4. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Store.hs:1247 and Commands.hs:367-388: the failure reply runs in the rollback handler outside boundedWith with the database lock held, and the receipt append after COMMIT has no bound. Fix: bound both appends, or document why they need no bound.

5. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Commands.hs:337: a failed append with ManagerFlowQuota refuses with StorageQuota, where the requirement says StorageUnavailable. COMMANDS.md documents the deviation. Fix: confirm the deviation or map it to StorageUnavailable.

6. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Commands.hs:220: checkFlowCeiling runs before checkRate, so a command that is over its rate and at the ceiling gets storage-quota instead of rate-limited. Fix: move the ceiling check after checkRate, or document the precedence.

7. (low) manager/test/CommandCheck.hs:1376: only the D3 (lossy codec) path tests the failure reply. Fix: add one commit-deadline-failure case in flow mode that asserts a failure reply with the matching refusal code.

Also from the implementer's limitations: on an uncertain COMMIT no failure reply is written (the missing reply denotes uncertainty), and a D3 mismatch refuses a Cancel as well.

Run both once.
5. (low) The documentation understates the acquisitions of each check (Authorization.hs:88-95, STORAGE.md:187-192). Reader admission takes the configuration guard and the Store gate, currentViewFacts takes the guard again, and observeAuthorizationAt takes the gate: two guard acquisitions and up to three gate acquisitions per write. The public 503 storage-unavailable is unchanged (ArtifactCheck.hs:671-679). Record the class change in the handoff or fault-classification notes if they list stream refusal classes.

* DONE [#C] DSL diagnostics: EOF at 0:0, positionless Chunk, arm-before-scrutinee ordering, misleading messages
:PROPERTIES:
:OBR_SCHEMA_VERSION: 17
:ID:       acat-bqx
:LABELS:   []
:ISSUE_TYPE: task
:CREATED:  [2026-08-14 Fri 19:00]
:MODIFIED: [2026-08-20 Thu 10:11]
:CREATED_BY: johnw
:FINISHED: [2026-08-20 Thu 10:11]
:CLOSE_REASON: done
:SOURCE_REPO: agent-cat
:SOURCE_REPO_PATH: /Users/johnw/src/agent-cat
:ORIGINAL_SIZE: 0
:END:

deep-review + alexey + validated. (1) End-of-input errors report 0:0 (Parse.lean:174-181), violating the one-based Pos contract; cli/AgentCat.lean:224-225 then drops the caret entirely — the commonest editing error (truncated file) gets the worst message. Fix: carry the end-of-source position. (2) Chunk.interp has no Pos (Syntax.lean:118-123), so every prompt error is reported at the enclosing ask (Check.lean:112-151) — in a language whose principal dataflow mechanism is interpolation. Fix: add Pos to Chunk.interp (the lexer knows it, Parse.lean:117-127). (3) ifFlag/caseVerdict elaborate all arms before checking the scrutinee's kind (Check.lean:392-426), so a wrong-kinded scrutinee reports an error from inside an arm. Fix: test bnd.at? first. (4) Panel monoid refusal names the first member's kind as everyone's (Check.lean:250-258). (5) Interpolation names lex as any run up to }/"/newline (Parse.lean:118), so non-identifiers surface later as 'unbound name' at the wrong place. (6) `up to 2 revision` and `up to 1 revisions` both parse (Parse.lean:430-435), defeating the two spellings' stated purpose.

1. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Routes.hs routeBatch, the FlowWindowBelowFloor branch when no cursor is supplied. The batch restarts at the reported floor on every below-floor refusal, with no limit. A floor that keeps rising would loop without end. Fix: add a restart counter (for example at most 4, as readManagerWindow uses) and refuse with cursor-expired or storage-unavailable after the limit.

2. (low) manager/test/service_http.py cases 12 and 13. The route test never seals or prunes inside the running manager. Case 12 renames the active file and case 13 unlinks the oldest segment while the manager is stopped, so cursor survival across rotation is shown only across a restart, and the segment-list retry of readManagerWindow (runtime Flow.hs:1031-1041) is not reached through the route. Fix: add a route test that seals while running, with a small segment size or a test hook, and walks one cursor across the seal.

3. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Routes.hs managerSource served. The profile lookups open one read transaction per window of up to 64 records, so one batch can open up to 16, not one as Events.visibleResources does. doc/api/README.md states the per-window behavior. Fix: do all lookups for the batch in one transaction, or accept and record the per-window behavior.

4. (low) manager/test/service_http.py record_owner (case 11). The oracle copies the owner rule of recordOwner. Case 7 and the independent SQLite owner set keep the test from being vacuous. Fix: optionally state the expected owner of each schema kind in the fixture, taken from the requirement text.

5. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Routes.hs recordOwner, FlowNotice branch. A command-changed, review-ended or request-ended notice whose body is stored as a claim check has no owner and becomes a filtered gap. It cannot happen at the current notice sizes. Fix: none now. Revisit if these notices can grow past the inline limit.

Non-blocking findings of the fess audit of Phase B part 2 subtask C17 (fail-over and dispatch-window
redirect through /v1, service_http.py mode controls-routing, and the steer and redirect ordering fix
in the runtime). Report: fess/b2-C17-r1.md in the private evidence directory.

1. (low) runtime/src/Agentic/Runtime/Machine.hs (about lines 327-337),
runtime/src/Agentic/Runtime/Control.hs (about lines 341 and 390-392), runtime/src/Agentic/Exec.hs
(about line 1117). The steer lock and the redirect "emitted" cell are released only when the receive
loop reaches afterAcknowledgement. If the sink throws while it emits AttemptSteered,
OccurrenceRedirected or the ack, closeAttemptSteering or awaitRuntimeRedirect blocks with no timeout
until the owner cancellation ends it. Fix: run the event emission and the ack under
`finally afterAcknowledgement` (or onException) in Machine.hs receive.

2. (low) manager/test/service_http.py (routing_cases, about lines 3957-4088) and
runtime/src/Agentic/Exec.hs (about lines 843-845). No configurable dispatch window exists. The test
relies on the automatic 30-second window for any question with more than one target, so the
fail-over case also waits the full window. Fix: accept this, or add a configurable or shorter window
to make the tests faster.

3. (low) manager/test/service_http.py (control_checks finally, about lines 4254-4262). Neither
controls nor controls-routing checks server-0.stderr for "class=store StoreIntegrity", the root
symptom of the race. The routing rerun also logged one GET /v1/runs/{id}/control 503
storage-unavailable class=store StoreBusy during polling. Fix: assert that no StoreIntegrity line
appears at the end of both modes, and triage the StoreBusy 503 on a GET.

4. (low) runtime/test/Main.hs (about lines 290-293 and 306-308). The ordering unit tests wait 50 ms
and then call tryReadMVar to show that a waiter has not finished. Under load they can miss a
regression. The test was not shown failing before the fix. Fix: add a deterministic check, for
example that the lock MVar is empty while the steer delivery is pending.

5. (low) runtime/src/Agentic/Runtime/Control.hs (about lines 437-446). The ACP 2-second steer-ack
timeout bounds the steer lock hold only for ACP. Nothing bounds the steer call of another
EngineSteerer, and the attempt end now waits on it. Fix: document the bound as specific to ACP, or
put a timeout around the steer call inside the lock.

Non-blocking findings of the fess audit of Phase B part 2 subtask C18 (increment 3, live re-route of an in-flight non-effect attempt in the runtime, difference D6). Report: fess/b2-C18-r1.md in the private evidence directory.

1. (medium) runtime/src/Agentic/Exec.hs (about lines 1127-1138), engine/acp/src/Agentic/Acp.hs (about lines 1570-1576). A live redirect stops the attempt with an asynchronous exception, but nothing calls cancelTurn, so the adapter keeps its prompt open until the engine shuts down. After a live redirect the run continues, so a real model keeps working on the stale turn, and a later question to the same engine in the same run could collide with it (late session/update chunks or a second session/prompt). No test covers this. Fix: send the engine turn cancel (cancelTurn or an engine-level equivalent) when AttemptRerouted stops an attempt, and add a probe step where a later question in the same run reuses the stopped engine.

2. (low) runtime/src/Agentic/Exec.hs (about line 1407). A re-route counts against the fail-over budget only because the stopped candidate leaves the chain walk (preferTarget target rest). No counter exists and the candidate is not marked spent. Design section 3.4 speaks of a bounded number. Fix: record the interpretation in the design record or runtime/BROKER.md, or add an explicit re-route count.

3. (low) runtime/src/Agentic/Exec.hs (about lines 1127-1160), design record section 3.4. The design says a late result of a stopped attempt is recorded as the reply to its turn. The implementation appends nothing from inside the stopped attempt, as the computed task text required. Fix: record the divergence as deferred, or reconcile the design record.

4. (low) runtime/src/Agentic/Runtime/Snapshot.hs (about line 390). The branch `Nothing | running -> redirected (DispatchSnapshot [target] False Nothing)` accepts any target without validation, and no test reaches it. Fix: add a snapshot history with no dispatch-pending event, or remove the branch if the runtime cannot reach it.

5. (low) cli/test/PolicyProbe.hs (about line 1595), runtime/BROKER.md (D6, last sentence). The PolicyProbe label "an active attempt cannot be redirected" is now true only when no live route is registered. BROKER.md names only the case live-redirect, while the refusals are the separate cases live-redirect-effect and live-redirect-outside. Fix: reword the label and name all three probe cases.

Also deferred from the implementer limitations: the manager does not offer or admit a live redirect through /v1 yet (manager/src/Agentic/Manager/State.hs about line 707 still requires an open dispatch window).

Design record: proposals/actor-flow-architecture-v2.md (revision 4) in the private resume-20260923 evidence directory. Non-blocking findings of the fess audit of Phase B part 2 subtask C20 (increment 3, the manager admits a live redirect through /v1). Report: fess/b2-C20-r1.md in the private evidence directory.

1. (medium) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/State.hs (about lines 749-760). liveRedirectTargets offers every approved route name, written on the occurrence addressee, for any running non-effect occurrence whose addressee has an '@'. This includes occurrences with no dispatch record (single-candidate questions in a routed profile), candidates earlier in the chain than the one in flight, and the candidate in flight after an automatic fail-over, because the current candidate is known only from dispatchRedirect or the authored candidate. The runtime rejects these with rejected-stale, so the control resource offers operations that cannot succeed. Fix: offer a live redirect only for an occurrence with a dispatch record, and only for targets after the candidate in flight in dispatchTargets order, or derive the targets from dispatchTargets.
2. (medium) manager/test/service_http.py (about lines 4162-4244). No /v1 case exercises a runtime rejection of a live redirect through the acknowledgement path. The effect case refuses at admission, and the single-route fixture always offers a live target. Fix: add a live-redirect case in which the runtime rejects an offered target (for example a two-route policy with a redirect to an earlier or exhausted candidate), and assert the rejected-stale acknowledgement and that nothing is re-routed.
3. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/State.hs (about lines 738-739). approvedRoutes maps a projectPolicy failure to an empty list with no signal. Approval.hs (about line 269) propagates the same failure. Fix: propagate the failure (for example throwIO StoreIntegrity).
4. (low) doc/api/openapi.yaml (about line 3636). The OccurrenceAddress description still says "pre-dispatch redirect", but a live redirect after the window now uses the same address. Fix: update the description (description-only, additive).
5. (low) doc/api/README.md (about line 400). The edited paragraph has one unwrapped line of about 110 characters. Fix: rewrap the paragraph.
6. (low) manager/test/service_http.py (about lines 4204-4222). Case 2 depends on the 8-second hold of hold-effect-adapter, which can become flaky under load. Fix: use a longer hold for the effect fixture, or a barrier that releases the effect attempt only after the refusal is checked.
7. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/State.hs (about line 756). T.breakOnEnd "@" gives wrong labels when an addressee or route name contains '@'. The runtime would reject those labels. Fix: derive the labels with the frontend candidate-label parser, or reject route names that contain '@' at policy validation.

Also deferred from the implementer limitations: the manager never offers a live redirect back to the default candidate, because the default route has no name in the policy. The new mode was not shown failing before the production change. Each check ran once, at N8 only.

Case 3 reads the adapter record with a silent fallback to an empty list when the file does not exist, so the no-session/prompt check would pass vacuously if the launcher never ran. Non-blocking findings of the fess audit of Phase B part 2 subtask C23 (WM-028 functional, worker death and manager/ci/supervision.sh, mode failures-worker of manager/test/service_http.py). Report: fess/b2-C23-r1.md in the private evidence directory.

1. (medium, functional) manager/test/service_http.py (about lines 4764-4783) and cli/src/Agentic/Cli/Frontend.hs (about line 129). The frontend proxy starts the inner frontend worker with inherited standard streams in a second process group. A SIGKILL of the proxy group alone leaves the inner group alive with the manager pipes open, so the manager does not observe the loss and the run stays under owned supervision. The failures-worker mode kills every descendant group, so it does not cover this case. Nobody checked whether a cancel, timeout or answer still reaches the inner worker after a proxy-only loss, or whether the inner group is orphaned after the proxy group cleanup. manager/WORKERS.md records the case as an instance of the escaped-descendant limit (WM-019 containment). Fix: reproduce by killing only the proxy group, then cancel the run and check for an orphaned inner group. Decide whether the proxy cleanup must signal the inner group, or whether the manager must watch the exit of its direct child.
2. (low) manager/test/service_http.py (about lines 4806 and 4809). Case 3 accepts any status other than 202 as a refusal, so a 400 or 500 would pass. The observed result was 409 ownership-unavailable for both commands. Fix: assert status 409 and code ownership-unavailable for the answer and the cancel.
3. (low) manager/test/service_http.py (about lines 4801-4805). If GET /v1/decisions/{id} does not return 200, the test does not send the answer and still passes. Fix: require status 200 for the decision read, or assert the specific expected code.
4. (low) manager/test/service_http.py (about line 4707). The variable terminal is defined and not used. Fix: remove it.
5. (low) manager/WORKERS.md (about lines 146-148). The section states the sequence owned, then cleanup-pending, then lost. The test observes only lost, 0.01 seconds after SIGKILL. Fix: observe cleanup-pending in a check, or state only what the check shows.

Non-blocking findings of the fess audit of Phase B part 2 subtask C24 (WM-028 functional, manager death and restart, mode failures-manager of manager/test/service_http.py). Report: fess/b2-C24-r1.md in the private evidence directory.

1. (medium, functional) manager/test/service_http.py (about lines 348-352), manager/CONFIGURATION.md (about line 90) and manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Credentials.hs (about line 184). After a manager crash, restart reconciliation quarantines the lost run's reservation, and the reservation keeps its execution slot and resource keys. The local administration operations check-quarantine and release-quarantine are refused with state-conflict (OtherAdmin), so nothing releases the quarantine. With the default executionReservations of 1, or with profiles that have no resource keys, no new run can start after a crash. The failures-manager mode passes "serves new work" only because its fixture adds a second reservation and a profile with its own resource key. This follows the existing WM-020/WM-042 design and is not a C24 regression. Fix: schedule the WM-042 quarantine inspection and release (cleanup evidence) as a functional item. Until it exists, state in manager/CONFIGURATION.md that a crash with one reservation blocks all later runs.
2. (medium) manager/test/service_http.py (about line 5095) and manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Store.hs (about lines 233-240). The case 4 assertion that the pruning round at open kept the lost run's segment has no positive control. It also passes if the pruner did not run, if the byte trigger did not hold, or if the round failed, because a prune failure becomes a recordFaultLine that nothing checks. Fix: seal an extra terminal-only segment (for example a withdrawn request) as the oldest segment, ahead of the lost run's segment, and assert that it is pruned while the lost-run segment stays. At a minimum, assert that no "manager-log prune" fault was recorded.
3. (low) manager/test/service_http.py (about lines 240 and 5055-5070). The harness seals the killed lifetime's manager log itself and splits it at the padding request's first record, while the writer splits by the size threshold S. The comment "as the writer seals it" holds only for the file format and naming. Fix: reword it to "in the writer's segment format", or reach a real seal through a smaller configured ceiling.
4. (low) manager/test/service_http.py (about lines 5175-5179). The exit status of the second manager lifetime is not asserted. SIGTERM ends it with returncode -2 through the SIGTERM-to-UserInterrupt path (cli/src/Agentic/Cli.hs, about lines 998-1001). Fix: assert second.returncode == -signal.SIGINT so that an unexpected crash of the second lifetime fails the mode.

Other C24 limitations recorded with the commit: the restarted manager does not ingest the on-disk evidence of the lost run (GET /v1/runs/{id} keeps runtime status running with lost supervision, as documented), and only N8 was run for the new mode.

Non-blocking findings of the fess audit of Phase B part 2 subtask C8 (positioned window reader for flow logs). Source:
/Users/johnw/Products/agent-cat-workflow-manager/implementation.9tGzKH/service-tui.purvEwEv/resume-20260923/fess/b2-C8-r1.md.

1. (medium) runtime/src/Agentic/Runtime/Flow.hs:1830 (doc at Flow.hs:1799 and runtime/BROKER.md:316). When a window has no records yet and the first complete line is longer than windowMaxBytes, the guard `used + index > windowMaxBytes limits` returns an empty window with windowMore set, so a caller that follows windowNext reads the same window forever. With the default limits, a line from maxFrameBytes+1 up to about maxFrameBytes+64 KiB whose newline arrives in the same piece takes this path, not FlowWindowUndecodable, which contradicts the documentation. The writer refuses such lines (Flow.hs:1152), so only a damaged log or a small caller-chosen byte bound reaches it. Fix: with no record decoded and index > maxFrameBytes, return FlowWindowUndecodable. With no record decoded and a line that exceeds only the caller bound, return that one record or refuse it, so that every window makes progress or refuses. Align the doc comment and BROKER.md.

2. (low) manager/test/Agentic/Manager/Test/FlowReader.hs:503. The check "the sealed segments of the window log are named by their start" compares only the number of directory entries with the segment count. Fix: compare the sorted names with map (flowSegmentName . segmentFirst) segments, or rename the check.

3. (low) manager/STORAGE.md:578. The storage reader paragraph describes readManagerLog but not readManagerWindow. Fix: add one sentence that names readManagerWindow and the floor it reports, or accept the link to BROKER.md.

Same shape as the served-by gap (acat-served-by-check-gap-i5d, fixed): mirror the parser's refusal in checkFnsList with the existing diagnosis wording, one hand-built battery case in the check_panel_nil style, audit the new site.

Non-blocking findings of the fess audit of Phase C subtask PC2 (WM-042 check-quarantine with cleanup evidence). Report: fess/pc-PC2-r1.md in the private resume-20260923 evidence directory.

1. (medium) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Quarantine.hs (about lines 156 and 237). No fixture reaches the cleanup-required branch (a launched run whose flow.ndjson has no stop) or the unverifiable branch for an unreadable run store. A regression that reports either one as clean would pass every check. Fix: add a CommandCheck or failures-worker fixture with a quarantined reservation whose run log has no stop and assert cleanup-required with null id, digest and expiresAt. Then remove or corrupt the run store and assert unverifiable.
2. (low) manager/test/CommandCheck.hs (about line 1080) and manager/test/service_http.py (about line 5270). The tests check only that expiresAt is a string. Fix: assert that expiresAt falls between the times taken before and after the call, plus cleanupEvidenceLifetime.
3. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Quarantine.hs (about lines 227-237). A runs row whose run store has no runtime directory or no flow.ndjson classifies as unverifiable, not cleanup-required. Fix: decide which state a missing run store gives, state it in manager/WORKERS.md, and add a fixture.
4. (low) manager/WORKERS.md (about line 225). The text says the facts are encoded "with its keys in order". The behavior and the harness depend on sorted key order. Fix: say "with its keys in sorted order".
5. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Quarantine.hs (about lines 140 and 167). processGeneration is read twice, once for the response and once for the facts. Fix: return the generation from inspectQuarantine and use that one value.
6. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Quarantine.hs (about lines 251-259). answered now also catches AdminFailure, which changes the error path of status and check-store too. Fix: confirm that this is intended, or catch AdminFailure only in checkQuarantine.

Further limitations recorded by the implementer: offline clean evidence through the CLI has no end-to-end test (only the unknown-id refusal offline); a Store integrity fault (two run rows for one reservation, or a start intent without a run) answers storage-unavailable, not unverifiable, with no fixture.

Non-blocking audit findings from B8 (WM-023 credential-lifecycle, fess report resume-20260923/fess/b1-B8-r1.md). The medium finding (reload-profiles refusal attributed to the serving manager instead of the administration command) was corrected in the B8 commit. Remaining low findings:

1. manager/COMMANDS.md states that rotation keeps the registered client, label, scopes and profiles, and that a replay executes nothing again. The credential-lifecycle mode asserts only clientId and scopes, and receipt identity on replay. Assert the label, the profiles and an unchanged operation count after the replay, or narrow the wording.
2. service_http.py stream_ends treats any EOF, ConnectionError or SSLError as an ended stream. Add a negative control that shows the stream survives one read deadline or heartbeat before revocation, and optionally check that server stderr records the unauthenticated end.
3. A scope change through reload-profiles is not exercised, because the administration command refuses reload-profiles. When reload-profiles or another scope-changing path exists, show that a retained page token returns 403 or 410 and the open stream ends on loss of profile access.
4. list-credentials has no rotation cutoff field, so the cutoff is shown only by timing. Keep as a recorded limitation unless an additive field is authorized.
5. A revocation that ends an SSE stream is logged as "manager-fault ... response GET /v1/events started public=401 unauthenticated class=command Unauthenticated". An expected authorization ending should not be classified as a manager fault (response logging owner).
6. The workflow check text for the command check needs work="$base/N8", because credential_cli.py requires the work directory to be named N1 or N8.
7. Untested: rotation changes the authorization revision, so the predecessor's open views probably end at rotation rather than at the cutoff. Test and document the actual behavior.

* DONE [#B] Order every question after the effects that precede it
:PROPERTIES:
:OBR_SCHEMA_VERSION: 17
:ID:       acat-effect-ordering-tr4t
:LABELS:   []
:ISSUE_TYPE: bug
:CREATED:  [2026-09-24 Thu 11:02]
:MODIFIED: [2026-09-24 Thu 11:13]
:CREATED_BY: johnw
:FINISHED: [2026-09-24 Thu 11:13]
:CLOSE_REASON: Every non-effect question waits behind the effect lane's tail (runtime/src/Agentic/Exec.hs watchLane). Pinned by three policy probes; all deterministic and documentation gates pass.
:SOURCE_REPO: agent-cat
:SOURCE_REPO_PATH: /Users/johnw/src/agent-cat
:ORIGINAL_SIZE: 0
:END:

A question that a Plan asks after an effect can be dispatched before that
effect completes. `runPlanIO` (runtime/src/Agentic/Exec.hs) starts each
occurrence as soon as the answers its prompt reads are ready. The write-effect
lane orders effects only among themselves, so a consult or observe that reads
nothing from an earlier act does not wait for it.

Reproduction: an act `tool "save" running ("sh", ["-c", "sleep 2; cat > capital.txt"])`
followed by `ask (tool "readback" running ("cat", ["capital.txt"]))`. The read
runs first and the run abandons with `cat: capital.txt: No such file or
directory`.

Required behaviour (owner decision, 2026-09-24): every occurrence that follows
an effect in plan order starts only after that effect has completed. Questions
between two effects remain concurrent with one another.

Done when the scheduler enforces the rule, a policy probe pins it with a slow
effect followed by a read, the manual states the rule, and the runtime gates
pass.

:PROPERTIES:
:OBR_SCHEMA_VERSION: 17
:ID:       acat-engine-owner-lock-coverage-9snr
:LABELS:   ["workflow-manager"]
:ISSUE_TYPE: task
:CREATED:  [2026-10-01 Thu 11:00]
:MODIFIED: [2026-10-01 Thu 11:16]
:CREATED_BY: johnw
:SOURCE_REPO: agent-cat
:SOURCE_REPO_PATH: /Users/johnw/src/agent-cat
:ORIGINAL_SIZE: 0
:END:

Later work under the PE2 owner decision of 2026-10-01 (option C). The run owner lock runs/<run>/owner.lock covers the inner frontend worker, plus any engine session that starts through Runtime ProcessGroup spawnSession (createProcessGroup), which inherits the lock through posix_spawn_file_actions_addinherit_np on macOS. The inner worker starts no engine that way today. ACP starts through System.Process.createProcess in connectAcp (engine/acp/src/Agentic/Acp.hs), agent-deck through withCreateProcess (engine/agent-deck/src/Agentic/AgentDeck.hs), and shell steps through readCreateProcessWithExitCode (runtime/src/Agentic/Runtime/Shell.hs). These processes do not hold the lock, so its absence proves only that the inner worker has ended.

Work: start the ACP and agent-deck engines through Runtime ProcessGroup sessions by way of a neutral spawn hook in engine/api (engine/acp/AGENTS.md forbids a runtime import), so that each engine session leader holds the owner lock. This changes engine signalling to session groups. Keep FD_CLOEXEC on owner.lock. Update manager/WORKERS.md ("Run directory owner lock") and runtime/README.md when the coverage changes.

Today both live engines bind EVERY addressee to one backend per run — run/Main.hs prints it as the contract: 'every addressee — model, tool and person — is this one adapter/session' (:590, :622). The Plan semantics already distinguish parties and servedBy alternates already record who answered, so a cross-model panel (gpt-5.5-pro AND gemini-3.1-pro judging the same patch in ONE run) is expressible but not executable. This is the single capability PAL MCP has that agent-cat cannot yet execute (doc/research/pal-vs-agent-cat.md). Design sketch: a party→backend routing table on the run (e.g. --route 'reviewer-secure=acp:codex' --route 'reviewer-simple=deck:PANE', default route for the rest), engine header naming every route, trace scope unchanged (it already records the answering party). Fail-over alternates then become cross-backend for free. With this landed, PAL MCP is fully subsumed by workflows + engine config.

:CLOSE_REASON: findPackage now walks the enclosing node_modules directories from the resolved pi-coding-agent, as Node resolution does. Against the Pi fork, npm run check passes and npm test passes all 10 files (89 tests). A simulated registry layout with pi-client hoisted and chord nested also loads. npm run test:integration passes its 4 vitest files (8 tests), and pi-remote-current.mjs passes with a short TMPDIR (see acat-n98b).
:SOURCE_REPO: .
:ORIGINAL_SIZE: 0
:END:

ext-pi/src/pi-remote-runtime.mjs found pi-client and chord only as siblings of the resolved pi-coding-agent directory or inside that package's own node_modules. Node resolves a linked package to its real path, and a Pi workspace keeps its packages in the checkout's root node_modules, so linking ext-pi to the Pi fork at ~/src/fork/pi made test/extension.test.ts fail with "Pi runtime package pi-client is unavailable". The lookup should walk the enclosing node_modules directories as Node does, which covers both the registry layout and a workspace checkout.
