Non-blocking findings of fess audit fess/pd-PD20-r1.md (2026-10-02) on subtask PD20 (WM-031 part 2, agent-workflows emacs-native, setup, captures, request and review in Emacs service mode). The emacs-native commit of PD20 names this issue.

1. (medium) emacs/wf-manager.el defconst wf-manager-capture-bytes and wf-manager-session-prepare-capture. The capture limit is the constant 67108864, but its docstring says that it is the captureBytes limit of the capabilities. ext-pi prepareCapture (ext-pi/src/manager/session.ts) reads limits.captureBytes from the capabilities and refuses when that limit is absent. With a manager that advertises a smaller limit, the Emacs client sends the upload and the manager refuses it. Fix: read limits.captureBytes from the session capabilities, as ext-pi does, or correct the docstring and the README entry to say that the limit is fixed.

2. (low) emacs/wf.el wf-refresh. The docstring says only "Forget every cached row listing". In service mode the command reads the request of a setup form again and redraws the form, and outside a setup form it shows a message. Fix: add a service-mode paragraph to the docstring that matches the README row.

3. (low) manager/test/service_http.py step 12 (serviceRunRefusal is None) and emacs/wf-manager-live.el. The assertion that the refusal is null after C-g cannot tell "C-g ended wf-run" apart from "wf-run returned silently". The receipt and request-set comparisons prove that step 12 sent no command. Fix: record a positive signal that wf-run stopped at the workflow prompt (for example an advice counter on wf-service--create equal to zero), or soften the PASS 12 wording.

4. (low) emacs/wf-service.el wf-service--settle, wf-service--await-review and wf-service--await-run. wf-run and the approve, discard and withdraw keys poll synchronously for up to 120 seconds inside the command. Fix: follow the request asynchronously through the session follow loop with the session-invalidation work of WM-031.

5. (low) emacs/wf-service.el wf-service-review-text. The docstring says that the text is the review as reviewLines of ext-pi/src/manager-ui.ts shows it, but the header line is Emacs's own. Fix: align the header with ext-pi reviewLines, or state in the docstring that only the consent facts mirror reviewLines.

6. (gap) PD/PD20/impl-r1/emacs-client.log. The final live emacs-client run predates the last edit of wf-manager-live.el, which the implementer calls comment-only. The audit rerun of ci/emacs.sh passed. Real queue positions and blocking reasons are checked only offline. Fix: none required; a later emacs-client run covers it.

Implementer limitations recorded with PD20: an uncertain create, capture, set-input, enqueue, approve, discard or withdraw stops with a message and is not reconciled through wf-manager-session-reconcile yet; a 412 on set-input does not reopen the setup form with its draft; a cancelled setup form leaves its request as a draft; the setup form and the review buffer refresh only on request.

Adopted from the web survey (comparison judge). (1) CONTRACT: name the checker's five refusal clauses as an advertised validation contract (Microsoft Agent Framework precedent): every hole names a live binder or earlier define of the right kind; every branch scrutinee is flag/verdict with all arms written in order; every binder's kind matches its source; no live name introduced twice and no binder spells a define; known-here matches Gamma. (2) HAZARDS, named not fixed: (a) panel annihilation — a declined member zeroes objections so {why.reasons} is legitimately empty (Inspect AI's 'collect' reducer is the shape of an eventual monoid-side fix; see acat-88m); (b) arms export nothing — a binding inside a branch arm cannot reach the join, a PRINCIPLED refusal (a value exported from an arm has a sum type and Ctx holds Codes); (c) the kind is the shape, the spec define is a courtesy — flag is what the adapter must satisfy, flagSpec is words helping the addressee produce it, and they can drift (PDL derives the constraint from the type; that is an adapter-layer fix). (3) DETERMINISM AS LAW: given the same answer sheet the run is the same — free here since meaning is a function on total sheets; MAF needs a Pregel barrier to approximate it; say it out loud because the field taught users nondeterminism. (4) EDIT-PRESERVATION, honest form: editing a question's WORDS changes its index into Omega (answers not preserved); what IS preserved is the shape sequence and the cost tree — the user-visible payoff of shape-as-data and what define buys (editing verdictSpec moves no binding and no cost node). (5) Two review criteria as standing rules (YAWL OR-join cautionary tale): no former's enablement may depend on state outside its own subterm; a construct whose cost is not readable from its own syntax must show it in the notation. (6) One-sentence docs items: per-iteration questions are distinct by unrolling (memoization does not collapse rounds); 'all must approve' is the named-reducer pattern at set size one and the comma slot is reserved for the day a second verdict combiner exists (PoLL evidence).

:PROPERTIES:
:OBR_SCHEMA_VERSION: 17
:ID:       acat-ftw9
:LABELS:   ["workflow-manager"]
:ISSUE_TYPE: task
:CREATED:  [2026-09-24 Thu 09:19]
:MODIFIED: [2026-09-30 Wed 22:24]
:CREATED_BY: johnw
:SOURCE_REPO: agent-cat
:SOURCE_REPO_PATH: /Users/johnw/src/agent-cat
:ORIGINAL_SIZE: 0
:END:

A5 fess round 2 (fess/A-A5-r2.md), medium, design risk. After association, every one-second tick starts a PageSetRead whenever no ticket is held (tui/src/Agentic/Tui/App.hs near 446, 242 and 695), and ServiceLane.mutationAdmission (tui/src/Agentic/Tui/ServiceLane.hs near 350-355) defers every new-mutation key while such a read is in flight. With a slow manager, a page-set read is in flight almost continuously, so the post-association mutation keys that A7, A8 and A10 add could be deferred repeatedly. No measurement records the page-set read duty cycle.

Acceptance: before A7 starts, a recorded specification decision states either that refresh pauses while a deferral outcome is shown or that a key waits for the current read to finish. The A6 journey measures how often a page-set read is in flight after association, and a model test covers the chosen rule.

Plan SHA-256: 80d0fc1f5785d1ba18136c840492f83d8920ea33d67e609c44f098f5d7c5ebf6

| G0: implementation baseline | Exact source/toolchain provenance, owner agreement, compatibility fixtures, package/import rules, and the accepted API/state contract are recorded. | WM-001 through WM-007. |

This is an independent evidence gate, not another implementation. Check the actual integrated source, theorem/axiom output, applicable deterministic/failure/platform/client tests, and compatibility. Do not close merely because prerequisite issues are closed. Preserve all stated evidence ceilings. No deployment or publication is authorized by this gate.

Global invariants:
| I01 | Agent-cat is the sole workflow interpreter. The manager does not compute answers, bills, memoization, routing decisions, or authored traces independently. | WM-004, WM-005, WM-015, WM-022, WM-040. |
| I02 | Requests, admission, live preparations, runtime status, supervision, pending decisions, and result verification are separate dimensions. | WM-004, WM-009, WM-013 through WM-018. |
| I03 | Only the exact live prepared worker can consume an approval. Changed inputs, profile, worker, or process generation require fresh preparation and consent. | WM-012, WM-014, WM-020, WM-027. |
| I04 | A manager-owned control pipe outlives any HTTP/SSE connection. Network disconnection does not become control EOF. | WM-012, WM-019, WM-026, WM-039. |
| I05 | Durable acceptance, attempted delivery, runtime acknowledgement, control effect, and terminal outcome are distinct facts. Ambiguous effects are not automatically replayed. | WM-010, WM-014 through WM-016, WM-020, WM-027. |
| I06 | Mandatory decisions use one per-run FIFO reservation mechanism across every endpoint. Controls retain exact occurrence, attempt, and correlation identity. | WM-016, WM-027, WM-039. |
| I07 | Stored paths, root identities, native IDs, PIDs, and invocation metadata do not confer execution or signalling authority. | WM-008, WM-012, WM-018 through WM-020, WM-024. |
| I08 | Initial inputs retain their literal/captured representation and byte contract. Typed runtime answers retain false, null, structured values, and runtime decoding. | WM-005, WM-011, WM-016, WM-029 through WM-038. |
| I09 | Artifacts are verified through retained trusted references before any successful content response. Export remains exclusive and confined. | WM-007, WM-017, WM-018, WM-025, WM-027. |
| I10 | Coordination state and invalidations commit together. Runtime sequence validation remains independent of manager commit order. | WM-009, WM-010, WM-015, WM-025, WM-026. |
| I11 | Replay has an explicit retained prefix. Snapshot boundaries, open-stream eviction, duplicate handling, and client refresh ordering cannot silently lose state. | WM-021, WM-025, WM-026, WM-029, WM-039. |
| I12 | Every application operation is authenticated and authorized. The only unauthenticated CORS exception is a bounded non-resource preflight check. | WM-023, WM-024, WM-027, WM-028. |
| I13 | Credential rotation preserves the registered client's mutation ledger. Backup restoration invalidates old authority and never treats lost receipts as unexecuted work. | WM-010, WM-020, WM-023, WM-028. |
| I14 | Resource bounds are enforced before large allocation and at global as well as client/profile boundaries. Safety supervision survives ordinary queue saturation. | WM-007, WM-009 through WM-013, WM-019, WM-021, WM-024 through WM-028. |
| I15 | Existing descriptor, session, protocol, control, manifest, store, and CLI branches retain their meaning. Client local mode does not silently become service mode. | WM-003, WM-005, WM-006, WM-018, WM-029 through WM-038. |
| I16 | Mathematical proofs, deterministic tests, platform tests, cross-machine tests, and deployment evidence have separate stated ceilings. | WM-004, WM-022, WM-039 through WM-044. |

** Acceptance Criteria

Exact source/toolchain provenance, owner agreement, compatibility fixtures, package/import rules, and the accepted API/state contract are recorded. Actual evidence and independent verification are recorded. No unavailable check is reported as green.

Plan SHA-256: 80d0fc1f5785d1ba18136c840492f83d8920ea33d67e609c44f098f5d7c5ebf6

| G1: isolated manager core | Real deterministic frontend workers complete the entire lifecycle under the manager without a network listener. Crash, cleanup, controls, history, and artifact evidence are exercised. | WM-008 through WM-022. |

This is an independent evidence gate, not another implementation. Check the actual integrated source, theorem/axiom output, applicable deterministic/failure/platform/client tests, and compatibility. Do not close merely because prerequisite issues are closed. Preserve all stated evidence ceilings. No deployment or publication is authorized by this gate.

Global invariants:
| I01 | Agent-cat is the sole workflow interpreter. The manager does not compute answers, bills, memoization, routing decisions, or authored traces independently. | WM-004, WM-005, WM-015, WM-022, WM-040. |
| I02 | Requests, admission, live preparations, runtime status, supervision, pending decisions, and result verification are separate dimensions. | WM-004, WM-009, WM-013 through WM-018. |
| I03 | Only the exact live prepared worker can consume an approval. Changed inputs, profile, worker, or process generation require fresh preparation and consent. | WM-012, WM-014, WM-020, WM-027. |
| I04 | A manager-owned control pipe outlives any HTTP/SSE connection. Network disconnection does not become control EOF. | WM-012, WM-019, WM-026, WM-039. |
| I05 | Durable acceptance, attempted delivery, runtime acknowledgement, control effect, and terminal outcome are distinct facts. Ambiguous effects are not automatically replayed. | WM-010, WM-014 through WM-016, WM-020, WM-027. |
| I06 | Mandatory decisions use one per-run FIFO reservation mechanism across every endpoint. Controls retain exact occurrence, attempt, and correlation identity. | WM-016, WM-027, WM-039. |
| I07 | Stored paths, root identities, native IDs, PIDs, and invocation metadata do not confer execution or signalling authority. | WM-008, WM-012, WM-018 through WM-020, WM-024. |
| I08 | Initial inputs retain their literal/captured representation and byte contract. Typed runtime answers retain false, null, structured values, and runtime decoding. | WM-005, WM-011, WM-016, WM-029 through WM-038. |
| I09 | Artifacts are verified through retained trusted references before any successful content response. Export remains exclusive and confined. | WM-007, WM-017, WM-018, WM-025, WM-027. |
| I10 | Coordination state and invalidations commit together. Runtime sequence validation remains independent of manager commit order. | WM-009, WM-010, WM-015, WM-025, WM-026. |
| I11 | Replay has an explicit retained prefix. Snapshot boundaries, open-stream eviction, duplicate handling, and client refresh ordering cannot silently lose state. | WM-021, WM-025, WM-026, WM-029, WM-039. |
| I12 | Every application operation is authenticated and authorized. The only unauthenticated CORS exception is a bounded non-resource preflight check. | WM-023, WM-024, WM-027, WM-028. |
| I13 | Credential rotation preserves the registered client's mutation ledger. Backup restoration invalidates old authority and never treats lost receipts as unexecuted work. | WM-010, WM-020, WM-023, WM-028. |
| I14 | Resource bounds are enforced before large allocation and at global as well as client/profile boundaries. Safety supervision survives ordinary queue saturation. | WM-007, WM-009 through WM-013, WM-019, WM-021, WM-024 through WM-028. |
| I15 | Existing descriptor, session, protocol, control, manifest, store, and CLI branches retain their meaning. Client local mode does not silently become service mode. | WM-003, WM-005, WM-006, WM-018, WM-029 through WM-038. |
| I16 | Mathematical proofs, deterministic tests, platform tests, cross-machine tests, and deployment evidence have separate stated ceilings. | WM-004, WM-022, WM-039 through WM-044. |

** Acceptance Criteria

Real deterministic frontend workers complete the entire lifecycle under the manager without a network listener. Crash, cleanup, controls, history, and artifact evidence are exercised. Actual evidence and independent verification are recorded. No unavailable check is reported as green.

This is an independent evidence gate, not another implementation. Check the actual integrated source, theorem/axiom output, applicable deterministic/failure/platform/client tests, and compatibility. Do not close merely because prerequisite issues are closed. Preserve all stated evidence ceilings. No deployment or publication is authorized by this gate.

Global invariants:
| I01 | Agent-cat is the sole workflow interpreter. The manager does not compute answers, bills, memoization, routing decisions, or authored traces independently. | WM-004, WM-005, WM-015, WM-022, WM-040. |
| I02 | Requests, admission, live preparations, runtime status, supervision, pending decisions, and result verification are separate dimensions. | WM-004, WM-009, WM-013 through WM-018. |
| I03 | Only the exact live prepared worker can consume an approval. Changed inputs, profile, worker, or process generation require fresh preparation and consent. | WM-012, WM-014, WM-020, WM-027. |
| I04 | A manager-owned control pipe outlives any HTTP/SSE connection. Network disconnection does not become control EOF. | WM-012, WM-019, WM-026, WM-039. |
| I05 | Durable acceptance, attempted delivery, runtime acknowledgement, control effect, and terminal outcome are distinct facts. Ambiguous effects are not automatically replayed. | WM-010, WM-014 through WM-016, WM-020, WM-027. |
| I06 | Mandatory decisions use one per-run FIFO reservation mechanism across every endpoint. Controls retain exact occurrence, attempt, and correlation identity. | WM-016, WM-027, WM-039. |
| I07 | Stored paths, root identities, native IDs, PIDs, and invocation metadata do not confer execution or signalling authority. | WM-008, WM-012, WM-018 through WM-020, WM-024. |
| I08 | Initial inputs retain their literal/captured representation and byte contract. Typed runtime answers retain false, null, structured values, and runtime decoding. | WM-005, WM-011, WM-016, WM-029 through WM-038. |
| I09 | Artifacts are verified through retained trusted references before any successful content response. Export remains exclusive and confined. | WM-007, WM-017, WM-018, WM-025, WM-027. |
| I10 | Coordination state and invalidations commit together. Runtime sequence validation remains independent of manager commit order. | WM-009, WM-010, WM-015, WM-025, WM-026. |
| I11 | Replay has an explicit retained prefix. Snapshot boundaries, open-stream eviction, duplicate handling, and client refresh ordering cannot silently lose state. | WM-021, WM-025, WM-026, WM-029, WM-039. |
| I12 | Every application operation is authenticated and authorized. The only unauthenticated CORS exception is a bounded non-resource preflight check. | WM-023, WM-024, WM-027, WM-028. |
| I13 | Credential rotation preserves the registered client's mutation ledger. Backup restoration invalidates old authority and never treats lost receipts as unexecuted work. | WM-010, WM-020, WM-023, WM-028. |
| I14 | Resource bounds are enforced before large allocation and at global as well as client/profile boundaries. Safety supervision survives ordinary queue saturation. | WM-007, WM-009 through WM-013, WM-019, WM-021, WM-024 through WM-028. |
| I15 | Existing descriptor, session, protocol, control, manifest, store, and CLI branches retain their meaning. Client local mode does not silently become service mode. | WM-003, WM-005, WM-006, WM-018, WM-029 through WM-038. |
| I16 | Mathematical proofs, deterministic tests, platform tests, cross-machine tests, and deployment evidence have separate stated ceilings. | WM-004, WM-022, WM-039 through WM-044. |

** Acceptance Criteria

Emacs, TUI, and Pi service modes pass their native UI gates and cross-client/cross-machine acceptance while local modes remain intact. Actual evidence and independent verification are recorded. No unavailable check is reported as green.

| I03 | Only the exact live prepared worker can consume an approval. Changed inputs, profile, worker, or process generation require fresh preparation and consent. | WM-012, WM-014, WM-020, WM-027. |
| I04 | A manager-owned control pipe outlives any HTTP/SSE connection. Network disconnection does not become control EOF. | WM-012, WM-019, WM-026, WM-039. |
| I05 | Durable acceptance, attempted delivery, runtime acknowledgement, control effect, and terminal outcome are distinct facts. Ambiguous effects are not automatically replayed. | WM-010, WM-014 through WM-016, WM-020, WM-027. |
| I06 | Mandatory decisions use one per-run FIFO reservation mechanism across every endpoint. Controls retain exact occurrence, attempt, and correlation identity. | WM-016, WM-027, WM-039. |
| I07 | Stored paths, root identities, native IDs, PIDs, and invocation metadata do not confer execution or signalling authority. | WM-008, WM-012, WM-018 through WM-020, WM-024. |
| I08 | Initial inputs retain their literal/captured representation and byte contract. Typed runtime answers retain false, null, structured values, and runtime decoding. | WM-005, WM-011, WM-016, WM-029 through WM-038. |
| I09 | Artifacts are verified through retained trusted references before any successful content response. Export remains exclusive and confined. | WM-007, WM-017, WM-018, WM-025, WM-027. |
| I10 | Coordination state and invalidations commit together. Runtime sequence validation remains independent of manager commit order. | WM-009, WM-010, WM-015, WM-025, WM-026. |
| I11 | Replay has an explicit retained prefix. Snapshot boundaries, open-stream eviction, duplicate handling, and client refresh ordering cannot silently lose state. | WM-021, WM-025, WM-026, WM-029, WM-039. |
| I12 | Every application operation is authenticated and authorized. The only unauthenticated CORS exception is a bounded non-resource preflight check. | WM-023, WM-024, WM-027, WM-028. |
| I13 | Credential rotation preserves the registered client's mutation ledger. Backup restoration invalidates old authority and never treats lost receipts as unexecuted work. | WM-010, WM-020, WM-023, WM-028. |
| I14 | Resource bounds are enforced before large allocation and at global as well as client/profile boundaries. Safety supervision survives ordinary queue saturation. | WM-007, WM-009 through WM-013, WM-019, WM-021, WM-024 through WM-028. |
| I15 | Existing descriptor, session, protocol, control, manifest, store, and CLI branches retain their meaning. Client local mode does not silently become service mode. | WM-003, WM-005, WM-006, WM-018, WM-029 through WM-038. |
| I16 | Mathematical proofs, deterministic tests, platform tests, cross-machine tests, and deployment evidence have separate stated ceilings. | WM-004, WM-022, WM-039 through WM-044. |

Final acceptance matrix:
| A01 | Create a request with several missing inputs. Empty text is present, null-as-text refuses, duplicate/unknown names refuse, and readiness creates no engine work. | WM-011, then WM-027 and all client gates. |
| A02 | Upload Unicode/CRLF/trailing-LF bytes, mutate the original file, and prepare. Captured digest and resulting semantic input remain exact. Exercise inline JSON expansion and the server-owned large-file path. | WM-005, WM-011, WM-022, then WM-028. |
| A03 | Enqueue competing shared/independent profiles at maximum reservations. Confirm FIFO eligibility, no partial-resource deadlock, review occupancy, and cleanup-based release. | WM-013, WM-019, WM-041. |
| A04 | Edit/expire/revoke a preparation or kill its worker before approval. An old digest/ETag cannot start a replacement worker. Restart requires a new review. | WM-014, WM-020, then WM-028. |
| A05 | Commit start intent and lose the HTTP reply or kill the manager around pipe delivery. Exact retries return the same receipt and no second start is attempted. Ambiguity remains explicit. | WM-010, WM-014, WM-020, WM-028. |
| A06 | Run two workflows with active attempts and mandatory decisions simultaneously. Show both dimensions, choose another run, and reject a non-head answer through every endpoint. | WM-015, WM-016, WM-027, WM-039. |
| A07 | Race two clients answering the same generation with false/null/structured data. One reservation wins, typed bytes remain correct, stale/unsupported/failed delivery is distinguished, and timeout does not allow a second answer. | WM-016, WM-028, WM-039. |
| A08 | Exercise retry, failover, abandon, redirect, both steering timings, and cancellation. Exact control IDs and occurrence/attempt effects correlate, including `occurrence.retried`. | WM-016, all native UI gates. |
| A09 | Close all network clients during active work and outstanding decisions. Work remains owned, decisions remain pending, and another authorized client can reconnect. | WM-012, WM-026, WM-039. |
| A10 | Send duplicate/gapped/wrong-run/conflicting envelopes and terminal events without valid authored trace. Preserve valid state and refuse invalid transitions without manufactured success. | WM-006, WM-015, WM-022, WM-040. |
| A11 | Report runtime success but remove/corrupt its result. Show terminal status separately from unavailable content. Verify a known good artifact despite journal corruption. | WM-017, WM-025, WM-028. |
| A12 | Replace state/export roots and race identical export names. At most one complete exclusive publication wins, existing bytes remain unchanged, and lost receipts never cause overwrite. | WM-007, WM-017, WM-028. |
| A13 | Restart/resume/fork legacy/v2/v3 parents with typed drop/replacement edits. Preserve parent facts and refuse invocation mismatch, live ownership, or quarantined resources. | WM-018, WM-020, WM-022, WM-040. |
| A14 | Attach SSE at a snapshot boundary while commits occur. Reconnect after a partial block, evict unseen events during an open stream, and expire detail pages. Apply complete events or resnapshot without gaps. | WM-025, WM-026, WM-028, WM-039. |
| A15 | Delay GET responses and resnapshot/switch endpoints while they are pending. Old responses/page sets cannot overwrite a newer fetch generation. Opaque ETags are never numerically sorted. | WM-029, WM-030, WM-033, WM-036. |
| A16 | Revoke/rotate credentials during POST, artifact download, pagination, and SSE. Preserve registered-client idempotency across rotation, revoke ongoing access, and fence later intents. | WM-023, WM-028, WM-039. |
| A17 | Restore an older backup after accepted operations and revocations. Old credentials, cursors, and authority keys fail. No unresolved old operation is reissued under a new key automatically. | WM-020, WM-028, WM-039. |
| A18 | Send allowed/forbidden CORS preflights, missing/forged Origin, unexpected Host, bypassed proxy headers, and redirects. Policy-only preflight reveals no resource, and actual access remains authenticated. | WM-024, WM-028. |
| A19 | Saturate uploads/drafts/event streams/page sets/commands and fill the DB disk. Refuse normal work honestly, keep bounded safety supervision available, and never acknowledge an uncommitted cancellation. | WM-019, WM-021, WM-028, WM-041. |
| A20 | Kill manager/worker/group leader and exercise escaped descendants on Linux and macOS. Prove containment or quarantine affected resources, never signal a recycled stored PID. | WM-019, WM-020, WM-041, WM-043. |
| A21 | Inject synthetic tokens, prompts, answers, provider diagnostics, HTML, and terminal escapes into failure paths. Incidental logs/URLs/argv remain clean and displays remain safe. | WM-008, WM-017, WM-023, WM-028, native UI gates. |
| A22 | Perform real keyboard interaction at three terminal sizes, preserving setup/review/answer/control drafts across resize and reconnect. Terminal/windows/focus are restored. | WM-032, WM-035, WM-038. |
| A23 | Create in one client, approve/answer in another, observe in a third across a real machine boundary, then disconnect/reconnect and verify lineage/results. | WM-039. |
| A24 | Upgrade and roll back a manager candidate with pending and completed work. Preserve compatible read-only history, reject incompatible DB versions, and retain explicit local client mode without live ownership transfer. Run local startup/pruning against distinct fixture roots and prove that manager records, lineage parents, and partial directories remain untouched. | WM-008, WM-020, WM-038, WM-042, WM-043. |

** Acceptance Criteria

Full failure/capacity evidence, operational procedures, reproducible packages, rollback, documentation, and independent review are complete. Deployment remains an explicit operator action. Actual evidence and independent verification are recorded. No unavailable check is reported as green.

If the reload or the probe throws instead of returning Left, no receipt is appended and the reload is outcome-uncertain at the next open. The model has draw : Nat (model/Agentic/Core/Dsl/Syntax.lean:175), and the other decoders refuse a negative draw (dsl/src/Agentic/Raw.hs:308 natField, tui/src/Agentic/Tui/Service.hs:945 natural). 2. (low) runtime/test/FlowCodecTests.hs:127 refused asserts only isLeft. The final re-encoding check at World.hs:674 also refuses unknown fields and a differing code, so the tests still pass if the unknown-field check (World.hs:664) or the code check (World.hs:666) is removed. Assert on the refusal text for the unknown-field, differing-code and effect-intent controls.

The Flow line decoder (F3 or later) must refuse duplicate keys and non-canonical numbers and enforce the 1 MiB bound.

Program of record per the owner's resolution of acat-haskell-surface-ygy (2026-08-16). Haskell is the production implementation: the typed workflow library of haskell-question.md Part 1 (the attacked design — first-order Tmpl prompts via quasi-quoter, variable tokens not answers, Codensity-bindable helpers, Discardable statement discipline, Checked-consuming runPlan, positional verdict arms, lazy-stream budgets turning recursive builders into refusals) as the authoring surface, plus the evaluator/runner (backends, content-addressed leaf store with fork/resume, typed backend/model pairing, preflight — the §6.3 invariants: acts never cacheable, hits are Cached never Done, keys salted with backend+model, verify runs checks itself vs agentVerify trusting a claim). The Lean formalization is retained in full as the mathematical anchor (meaning = Ω → (A × Trace), proven); no .wf in production (surface frozen at round 16; r17/r18 pages remain design records with reopening conditions).

Phases:
1. CONNECTION RESEARCH (first gate): the four mechanisms — bespoke Lean→Haskell extractor for this first-order fragment; FFI-linking the Lean-compiled C core; Lean as a subprocess semantic engine; reimplementation + bisimulation — 2026 tooling reality, real costs, recommendation to the owner.
2. MOCK AGENT + BISIMULATION HARNESS (built regardless of 1): a shared scripted world both sides operate against; property tests (generated programs and worlds) comparing traces and bills between Lean's denote/trace and the Haskell evaluator; the harness is the permanent conformance boundary.
3. THE LIBRARY per Part 1, amended by phase 1's outcome (if extraction/FFI wins, the semantic core is generated/linked rather than written).
4. THE RUNNER (the shared floor + the store).
5. The serialized checked-term format for the MCP/agent-authoring surface (the prose surface stops being .wf; the replacement is the serialized first-order format checked by checkPlan — priced in the report).

The Lean-side queue (99n --session, then vv6 deck engine) proceeds against the existing agent-cat CLI as spec/test runner; their production equivalents land in phase 4.

Owner question (2026-08-16): the round-17/18 surface converges on Haskell. What would a Haskell library look like that offers a type for constructing these workflows plus a verified evaluator against a backend agent? Would it look like agent-functor (~/src/agent-functor: quasi-quoter for interpolating large strings into expression arguments), or can that design be improved? Deliverable: a deep-dive report (workflow: agent-functor autopsy + agent-cat guarantees inventory + prior-art sweep -> best-possible Haskell design + three-way comparison -> adversarial pass) informing whether to (a) continue the DSL project (round-18 campaign acat-r18-campaign-2s9 is gated and waiting), (b) switch to Haskell as surface syntax + typing discipline with QQ prompts, or (c) a hybrid (Haskell EDSL frontend elaborating to the Lean-verified kernel). Key theory to weigh: Applicative/Selective/Monad maps onto batch/branch/dynamic rungs (Mokhov's selective functors; Build Systems a la Carte's applicative-vs-monadic tasks = the level lattice); pipeline (static shape, value-dependent prompts) fits none of the classes directly and is where the Lean formers earn their keep; Haskell cannot restrict >>='s continuation, so Monad = dyn; 'verified evaluator' in pure Haskell is property-tested at best, so the honest options are Liquid Haskell, extraction pairings, or keeping Lean as the kernel. The recommendation is the owner's decision; the report must be honest about what each path loses.

Found by the connection-research attack pass (acat-lean-haskell-connection-lhi): heardMatchesReplay is decide (r.trace = rep.transcript) where r.trace = r.heard.map (.event) — deliver appends one Heard per SURFACED question and Dlg.resume walks past questions the table already answers, so arrivals are memo-deduped — while rep.transcript = Plan.trace (worldOf table) p Env.nil replays EVERY event including repeats. On a run with any repeated question (billMemo < billFresh), the check is an assertion of falsehood. Repair options: compare heard against the dedup of the replay (respecting Lean dedup keeping the LAST occurrence), or record the intended invariant differently. Add an McpSmoke case with a repeated question to pin whichever is chosen.

Follow-up from the F6 fess audit of bypass removal, pre-store control handoff and person-answer attribution (actor-flow delta 1a). None of these findings blocks. Source: fess audit /Users/johnw/Products/agent-cat-workflow-manager/implementation.9tGzKH/service-tui.purvEwEv/resume-20260923/fess/flow-F6-r1.md.

1. runtime/src/Agentic/Exec.hs (worldOfEngineBrokered, engineContextFor broker _ Nothing) and runtime/BROKER.md: no test exercises an engine ask without attempt context. BROKER.md says that flowBroker refuses such an ask before delivery, but only code reading supports this. Fix: add a runtime unit test that runs worldOfEngineBrokered over an unscoped flowBroker with worldAskIO and shows the refusal before the inner broker counts a brokerStart.
2. test/flow_probe.py (early-control scenario): the scenario uses time.sleep(0.5) so that the control arrives before the cell swap. On a slow machine the control can arrive after activation, and the check fails spuriously. Fix: wait for a deterministic condition, such as the early control acknowledgement, before stdin closes.
3. test/flow_probe.py (negative_control): the negative control removes a turn record only. Nothing shows that the control-record half of the structural check fails. Fix: add a second negative control that removes one control record from the person log and expects "has no control record".
4. test/flow_probe.py (allowlist): the allowlist matches (file, stripped text), not (file, line). A second line with identical text in the same file passes, and lines inside block comments are counted. Fix: key the allowlist by occurrence count per (file, text) or by line number, and skip block comments.
5. cli/test/RoutingFixedPointProbe.hs (ApprovalPhrase mode) and engine/api/src/Agentic/Engine.hs: the case of an engine that reports a different target is tested through narration text only, because EngineResult has no structured target field. No change now. Revisit when the engine result gains a reported-target field.
6. test/flow_probe.py (retry forms) and section 3.2 of the design record: the design text says that a transport-gap retry appears as a new engine-start and turn. The injected gap gives two engine-start records and one turn record, and the retry goes through an operator retryOccurrence control. Fix: inject the gap after the first turn starts, or state the difference in runtime/BROKER.md.

Worked example capital; policy, routing-config, ACP, examples, deck, tier0, and both doc gates pass.
:SOURCE_REPO: agent-cat
:SOURCE_REPO_PATH: /Users/johnw/src/agent-cat
:ORIGINAL_SIZE: 0
:END:

Allow a registered Haskell function to answer a question put to a named tool,
in the way that `executingWorld` answers a `running` tool by running a command.

The workflow term does not change. A workflow writes `ask (tool "shout")
[wf|{capital}|]`, and the runner answers that question from a table that maps
tool names to Haskell functions. A function receives the rendered prompt and
returns the answer at the question's code. The table is supplied by the
composition root, beside the program's registry entry, so that workflow sources
stay symbolic.

Done when the runtime has the layer, the CLI composes it for live runs, a probe
shows a function's answer flowing into a later prompt and an act-position
function ordered with other effects, the manual documents it, and the gates
pass.

3. (low) manager/test/service_http.py near lines 8487-8490 and 8618-8634: the journey does not resize every view. The Manager workflows browser appears only at 40x12 and is never resized, the history detail is not resized, and the decisions view is resized only while it is empty. (medium) bisim/manager/ManagerConformance/Codec.lean line 248, the history aggregate line of manager/test/ConformanceCheck.hs, and bisim/manager/README.md line 447: the oracle accepts every observation entry unconditionally (observe := some s). Across the 41 passing roots, 204 of the 283 accepted ledger commands are observations and only 79 are model transitions. Some roots, such as approval/changed-descriptor and approval/changed-input, have no ledger transition, so their ledger check cannot fail. Fix: print the transition and observation counts in the aggregate line, and state in the README limits that only approve commands and decision-answering commands are checked by the model and that an observation is accepted unconditionally.
2. (medium) manager/test/Agentic/Manager/Test/Conformance.hs lines 481, 604, 609, 797, 841, 861 and 892: the fold and the projection build reservation leases (reservationLease), consumed preparations and approve intents (preparedOf), and answer values (answerValue) with the same functions from the same rows, and the cleaned evidence comes from the encoder's own leases. The square therefore checks key sets, phases, FIFO order, delivery and the presence of requests.run, not independent content. Fix: add these identities to "Limits of the history lane", and add a control that mutates a compared content field (a slot or key of a held reservation, or a command delivery state) to show whether the lane detects it.
3. (low) manager/test/Agentic/Manager/Test/Conformance.hs line 613: answerValue falls back to fromMaybe "" (cmBodySha c), so a command with no control intent and no body SHA-256 gets the answer value "" on both sides and passes silently. Fix: emit Unencodable instead of the empty string.
4. (low) bisim/manager/README.md (Limits of the history lane): 38 of the 39 approvals in the vertical roots take their digest and revisions from the rows, because those roots keep no manager log. Fix: keep the disclosure, and optionally add a vertical fixture that keeps its manager log.

:PROPERTIES:
:OBR_SCHEMA_VERSION: 17
:ID:       acat-ki26
:LABELS:   ["review","workflow-manager"]

:MODIFIED: [2026-10-01 Thu 06:00]

Non-blocking findings of fess audit fess/pc-PC27-r1.md (2026-10-01) on subtask PC27 (WM-034 export from a run).

1. (medium) tui/test/ServiceTests.hs near line 468 (against tui/src/Agentic/Tui/App.hs near line 1244): the 412 model test exercises only the generic L.sendStep and an exportLines golden on an ExportRefused that the test builds itself. The App handleServiceSent branch that turns a 412 into the export line of the run is not exercised. Fix: extract the refusal-to-export-outcome mapping into a pure helper that App calls and test it, or drive a 412 through the App handler in a model test.
2. (medium) tui/src/Agentic/Tui/App.hs near lines 1122 and 1677: while an export is awaiting or uncertain with a location, refreshServiceRequest reads only the export receipt and replaces every composite read and result retrieval. If that read is refused on each refresh (size or digest mismatch from downloadVerified, or a receipt that is not published after the exported effect), the command never settles, the selection is not read again, and no new mutation can start. Fix: after a refused export receipt read, keep the composite read running or settle the command as unresolved, with its reason on the export line.
3. (low) tui/src/Agentic/Tui/App.hs near line 1699: the catch-all `_ -> put current` drops an ExportPublished whose command receipt fails receiptMatches, and each later refresh downloads the export again. Fix: show a mismatched published receipt as a refusal, or settle the command.
4. (low) tui/src/Agentic/Tui/ServiceLane.hs near line 470: a 409 state-conflict for an export name that another export holds goes down the generic uncertain path and offers an exact resend, and the export line shows nothing. A command-level refusal settles only through the status line. Fix: show export refusals other than 412 on the export line, and handle a definite 409 in the lane.
5. (low) tui/src/Agentic/Tui/Service.hs near line 400: the collection ETag is read inside the preparation step, immediately before the POST, not when the editor opens. The If-Match therefore carries no state that the operator saw, and a 412 is practically unreachable end to end. Fix: the operator decides whether the ETag must be read at editor open and kept with the editor state.
6. (low) manager/test/service_http.py near line 5698: the requirement said the exported bytes equal the result bytes. Under the frozen contract (doc/api/README.md near lines 86-88, manager/ARTIFACTS.md near line 34) an export is the compact code-and-value document plus LF, and the fixture checks against that document built from the verified result bytes. Fix: none in code; the reinterpretation is recorded here and in the WM-034 comment.
7. (low) doc/workflow-manager-handoff.md near line 1035: the handoff still lists "no history, lineage or export" and also denies cancel and steer. Fix: refresh that current-state paragraph when it is next touched.

Disclosed limitations of the implementer: e is offered only when the snapshot shows a verified result; the TUI keeps the outcome of the latest export only and does not list the existing exports of a run; tui/ci/tui.sh, ALLBUILD and the N=1 journey were not run.

Non-blocking fess findings of Phase C subtask PC4 (report: resume-20260923 fess/pc-PC4-r1.md).

Medium:
1. Store.hs administrationCommitted counts any reservation in state released as a committed release and any credential with revoked=1 as a committed revoke. No column records the command that caused the effect, so an orphaned release ask that would have been refused (for example a duplicate release) reads committed-receipt-lost. The failures-manager committed orphan is such a duplicate. Repair: record the releasing or revoking command id, or document that committed-receipt-lost means only that the effect is present.
2. Verification gap: a restart now appends one reply per unanswered ask. manager-admission-check, the default mode of manager-command-check, tui/ci/tui.sh, credential_cli.py and the other service_http.py modes were not run after PC4. Run them once and fix any record-count drift.

Low:
3. Store.hs answerOrphanedAsks: when the asks cannot be read, the fault line 'manager-log reconciliation stopped unreadable' omits the ManagerFlowFailure reason, and failed reply appends are discarded with void.
4. An undecodable ask body that names a command without a ledger row reads lifetime-ended even if it was an administration ask; it should read outcome-uncertain. answerOrphanedAsks replies to every ask schema without asserting FlowCommand.
5. manager/STORAGE.md Growth paragraph: 'A crash does not hold the floor in later lifetimes' goes too far, because a failed reply append or an unreadable log still holds the floor until a later lifetime.
6. doc/workflow-manager-handoff.md: the dated floor-stop finding row of the end-of-part review still describes the old behavior; mark it resolved at closeout.
7. A retired receipt gets a failure reply with receipt-expired, a fourth reason that the requirement did not name (documented in STORAGE.md).

* DONE [#B] A repeated question after an effect is answered from before it
:PROPERTIES:
:OBR_SCHEMA_VERSION: 17
:ID:       acat-memo-across-effect-bgyt
:LABELS:   []
:ISSUE_TYPE: bug
:CREATED:  [2026-09-24 Thu 11:13]
:MODIFIED: [2026-09-24 Thu 13:24]
:CREATED_BY: johnw
:FINISHED: [2026-09-24 Thu 13:24]
:CLOSE_REASON: An effect clears reuse: the runtime keys reusable answers and persisted answers by (epoch, bare question), and Lean's execAnnotated clears its table at an effect with billMemo counting per stretch between effects. Corpus byte-identical (193 re-observed); bisim 500/500; all deterministic and documentation gates pass.
:SOURCE_REPO: agent-cat
:SOURCE_REPO_PATH: /Users/johnw/src/agent-cat
:ORIGINAL_SIZE: 0
:END:

A consultation or observation is reused by bare question. When the same
question is asked before and after an effect, the second occurrence now waits
for the effect, and is then answered from the memo table with the reading taken
before the effect.

Example: `a <- ask (tool "r" running ("cat", ["f"]))`, then an act that
rewrites `f`, then the same `ask` again. The second answer equals the first,
although the file changed.

The memo policy is documented and `billMemo` prices it, so a change here is a
change to what the memo bill means. Options: key reusable answers by the number
of effects that precede them in plan order, or keep the policy and refuse or
warn when a reusable question repeats across an effect. Needs an owner
decision.

Follow-up from the F3 fess audit of Agentic.Runtime.Flow (actor-flow delta 1a). None of these findings blocks. Source: fess audit /Users/johnw/Products/agent-cat-workflow-manager/implementation.9tGzKH/service-tui.purvEwEv/resume-20260923/fess/flow-F3-r1.md.

1. (medium, documentation) The recFrom Haddock in runtime/src/Agentic/Runtime/Flow.hs (near line 166) says that the writer stamps the sender from its binding. The writer has no binding: appendAsk, appendTell and appendReply accept any Actor from the caller. The test "the sender is the writer's binding" in runtime/test/FlowTests.hs (near line 307) only checks that the argument comes back. Fix: reword the Haddock and the test label, or add the binding in F4 and state there that it arrives.
2. (medium, correctness) Design section 1.1 says that the schema fixes the codec of the body. checkBodyForm only tells event bodies from other bodies, and bodyFor accepts any value for every schema except event. The writer test appends a start record whose body is the string "start", which startFromBody refuses. Fix: make F4 carriage pass only typed bodies, or check the body codec in the writer and in decodeFlowLine for every schema that has no SCode. Change the fixture to use a real startBody.
3. (low) ChooseRecovery RecoveryRetry encodes as retryOccurrence and decodes as RetryOccurrence (Control.hs near lines 577-590), so the control body is not exact for that value. The tests leave the value out. Fix: add a test that states the collapse, or file the ambiguity in the control wire form.
4. (low) Neither steerBody nor appendAsk refuses a steer record whose About has no occurrence (Flow.hs near line 688). Fix: refuse such an append, or record that F4 enforces it.
5. (low) startInputBytes is an Integer, but its decoder accepts values only up to Int64 (Flow.hs near lines 970-971). A Start above 2^63 bytes encodes and appends, and then startFromBody refuses it. Fix: use Word64 or Int64, or refuse the value at encoding.
6. (low) writeClaim reuses an existing claim file when its bytes are equal (Flow.hs near lines 841-853). Nobody checked whether writePrivateExclusiveAt is atomic. If it is not, a partial file from a failed write blocks that digest permanently. Fix: confirm atomicity, or delete a partial claim file on failure.
7. (low, verification) ALLBUILD was not run for F3. Components outside agentic-run, runtime-contract-test and routing-fixed-point-probe were not compiled against the new Agentic.Runtime exports. Fix: run ALLBUILD once at integration of delta 1a.

* DONE [#D] The Pi remote-session integration script fails on macOS with the default TMPDIR
:PROPERTIES:
:OBR_SCHEMA_VERSION: 17
:ID:       acat-n98b
:LABELS:   []
:ISSUE_TYPE: bug
:CREATED:  [2026-09-24 Thu 16:49]
:MODIFIED: [2026-09-24 Thu 16:58]
:CREATED_BY: johnw
:FINISHED: [2026-09-24 Thu 16:58]
:CLOSE_REASON: pi-remote-current.mjs now creates its socket directory under /tmp, which keeps the socket path at 74 bytes. npm run check passes, and npm run test:integration passes with the default macOS TMPDIR: 4 vitest files (8 tests) and the remote-session script.
:SOURCE_REPO: .
:ORIGINAL_SIZE: 0
:END:

ext-pi/test/pi-remote-current.mjs puts its fixture server socket under mkdtemp(tmpdir()). On macOS the default TMPDIR under /var/folders makes the path 118 bytes, which exceeds the 104-byte limit for a Unix socket path. The server starts and the socket file exists, but the client's connect fails with ENOENT, and npm run test:integration exits 1. With TMPDIR=/tmp/claude-501 the script passes. Either the script should place the socket under a short directory, or the Pi client should connect to long paths as the listener binds them.

First slice is implemented: frontend-io reads one version-1 JSON request through stdin EOF, returns one JSON response/newline, and never creates roots, launches runs, or grants live controls. Operations are open-root, read-question, and read-result. Root identities are opaque captured directory identities. Verification delegates to Runtime.PrivateRoot and the existing descriptor-relative Store readers. No journal replay is needed for an artifact read. Requests are bounded at 2 MiB and responses at maxArtifactBytes plus 4096. Data/verification failures exit 3 with stderr diagnostics and no JSON response.

1. (low) emacs/wf-manager-live.el:166 and manager/test/service_http.py:10457. The report field scheme comes from the global defvar wf-manager--scheme ("https"), not from the URL that the transport used, so the harness assertion report["scheme"] == "https" is tautological. TLS is proven otherwise (https endpoint, TLS-only manager, successful binding). Fix: take the scheme from the transport request URL, or record the GnuTLS peer status of the connection, and have the harness assert that value.

2. (low, security, deferred under the 2026-09-30 functionality-first direction) emacs/wf-manager.el:3488 with 3654-3657. The transport binds network-security-level to low for its processes, so GnuTLS (gnutls-verify-error t, profile caFile as the only trust file) is the only trust check. No check shows that a wrong caFile is refused. Fix: in the security stage, add a live or offline negative check that a caFile without the server certificate fails the binding.

Non-blocking findings of fess audit fess/pd-PD14-r1.md (2026-10-02) on subtask PD14 (WM-030 part 7, agent-workflows emacs-native 543c16f).

1. (medium) emacs/wf-manager.el:3404,3497,3619-3650 and emacs/wf-manager-tests.el:1705. Every transport test binds wf-manager--scheme to "http", so the production https path (GnuTLS with gnutls-trustfiles set to the profile caFile, gnutls-verify-error t, and the NSM advice after the handshake) never runs. The NSM test calls wf-manager--nsm-verify directly. Fix: add one HTTPS exercise, a GET of /v1/capabilities against the local protected manager or a local TLS listener with a test CA, through wf-manager-connect in batch Emacs, that shows no prompt and a checked capability binding.
2. (low) emacs/wf-manager.el:3674,3708,4079. wf-manager--send pushes the exchange onto the transport before url-retrieve and catches only file-error. Another synchronous error leaves the exchange pending, so a later wf-manager-transport-close calls the callback a second time, and wf-manager-connect leaks its transport and temporary directory. Fix: remove the exchange (and close the transport in wf-manager-connect) on any other synchronous signal, or push the exchange only after url-retrieve returns.
3. (low) README.md:757 and emacs/wf-manager.el:3417,3614. The README says the session directory holds the NSM settings file and an empty url.el cache directory, but no code creates either one. Fix: say that the directory is where url.el and nsm would write these files, or create the cache directory in wf-manager-transport-open.
4. (low) emacs/wf-manager.el:3497. The global :around advice on nsm-verify-connection is added on each transport open and never removed. Fix: remove it when the last transport closes, or record why it stays in the module commentary.
5. (low) Evidence: the failing-first run is recorded only in impl-r1/notes.txt, with no saved log. Fix: keep a failing log in later rounds when one exists.

Follow-up from the F11 fess audit of the review and administration records (actor-flow delta 1b). None of these findings blocks. Source: fess audit /Users/johnw/Products/agent-cat-workflow-manager/implementation.9tGzKH/service-tui.purvEwEv/resume-20260923/fess/flow-F11-r1.md.

1. (medium) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Store.hs:1187-1198 and 1237-1262, manager/APPROVAL.md:71-72: appendReviewRecord records no pending state. After the review append, runWithAdmission still runs validateEvents, appendInvalidation, checkCommitDeadline and the admission-fence check before COMMIT. A definite rollback at any of these points leaves a synchronized review record for a preparation that was never published, and no record answers it. APPROVAL.md claims that each review record names the digest that its own commit publishes, which is false in this case. Fix: record pending state for the review so that a definite rollback appends a failure or notice that names the review position, as PendingCommand does, or correct APPROVAL.md and STORAGE.md. Add a flow-review case that forces a commit-check refusal after the append.

2. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Credentials.hs:95-106: recordAdministrationReceipt returns the original response when the decoded receipt differs or fails strict decoding, and writes no gap entry or notice. Fix: record a gap or notice for a receipt mismatch, or document why the fallback is correct.

3. (low) manager/test/CommandCheck.hs:1537 and 1548-1550, manager/COMMANDS.md:346-348: the documentation says that a rollback after a successful administration append adds a failure reply, but the test fault fires on the append itself. Fix: add a case that makes the transaction fail after the command append and checks the failure reply.

4. (low) manager/test/CommandCheck.hs:1580: the check that administrationReceiptFromFlowBody of each receipt equals Right of the same receipt only proves that the decoder accepts the body. Fix: compare the receipts with the expected frozen admin responses.

5. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Flow.hs:436-457: the administration body records the operator label. The design forbids only tokens, verifiers and paths, and the frozen admin response already carries the label. Fix: confirm that the label is acceptable, or remove it from the body.

6. (low) cli/test/ManagerApprovalProbe.hs:691-697: builtNative runs bash test/cabal.sh list-bin as a subprocess when NATIVE is omitted, so flow-review works only from the repository root. Fix: keep it as documented, or require NATIVE.

7. (low) manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Flow.hs:416-494: manager command records now have two body shapes, a /v1 command and an administration operation. Fix: the delta 1b manager-log reader must dispatch command bodies on the administration key.

Also from the implementer's limitations: if the COMMIT after a review append is uncertain, the review record stays in the log and no notice marks the case. The administration checks call administerCredentials directly on a serving Store and do not go through the local socket.

From the live re-test at 3b2ab57. (1) claude-agent-acp prepends model-fallback narration ('**Model fallback:** claude-fable-5 declined this request (cyber); retried with claude-opus-4-8') to the answer stream as ordinary agent_message_chunk text. In one run it was concatenated to a reviewer's 'APPROVE', and because approval must be the WHOLE reply (the fail-closed rule), decodeVerdict read the result as an objection and bought a revision round. Consider: strip a recognised leading narration block before decoding (fragile, and it is the adapter's text not the model's), or record it as a turn annotation, or leave decoding strict and surface the narration in the transcript so a reader knows why a verdict flipped. Note the substituted model (claude-opus-4-8) is NOT in the adapter's advertised catalogue, so Conn.configValues is not a complete account of what may answer. (2) Exec.say discards the usage object claude puts on the wire; capturing tokens per turn would let the runtime report real cost beside the tick bill, and would settle (3). (3) permissionByCode's docstring cites ~97k tokens as the measured cost of denial, but the live refusing run showed 0 extra turns and 0 retries — the figure came from an earlier probe under different conditions. Either measure it properly with usage data or soften the claim to what is known.

Both agree with the rule that the overview is read while its view is shown. Record as a known limitation; no change needed now.

Non-blocking findings of fess audit fess/pd-PD1-r1.md (2026-10-01) on subtask PD1 (ext-pi endpoint switch commits only after the new overview loads, item 1 and item 7 of acat-phase-e-review-findings-0l73).

1. Medium. ext-pi/src/manager/session.ts:898: the live predicate of switchEndpoint checks only that the session is open and that the transport is still the earlier one. If the follow loop of the earlier binding ends (refused or unreachable) while the new overview loads, the switch still commits. The new binding then has no follow loop, followEnd keeps the end of the earlier transport, and ServiceMode.#report returns kind 'failed' with the session still installed and open. The requirement states a failed selection with the session closed and no follow loop. 'connected' is never reported, and the next select recovers. Fix: add this.#followEnd === undefined to the live predicate, so that this case takes the close-and-fail branch at ext-pi/src/service-mode.ts:282-286, and add a unit case.
2. Low. ext-pi/src/service-mode.ts:282-286: no test runs the branch that closes the session and reports 'failed' when the earlier follow loop ended during a switch. Fix: add a unit case where the earlier transport ends its event stream (refused) while the new overview read is held, and assert kind 'failed', a closed session and no follow loop.
3. Low. ext-pi/src/manager/session.ts:662-664: the new #fetch generation guard has no test. The assertion that the new transport does not receive run_a1 (ext-pi/test/service-mode.test.ts:268) passes without the guard, because no fetch is queued when the switch commits. Fix: add a case that queues a watched-resource fetch of the earlier binding behind a held read, commits a switch, releases the read, and asserts that the new transport never receives the earlier resource.

The checks compare real id sets and receipt pairs, so they are not vacuous, but they are not proven against a fault. Fix: optionally add a control mode in which the script, or a modified Emacs hook, sends one extra command after the reconnect or at the view kill, and require that the mode fails with a literal message.

3. (low) manager/test/service_http.py emacs_lifecycle_checks. The restart child that remains after the manager restart keeps a quarantined reservation until the mode ends. The existing checks of the same fact use identity (service_http.py near 9288, 10338 and 10508). Fix: assert len(recorded) == 1 and recorded[0] is False.
3. (low) ext-pi/src/manager/session.ts near 684-685: send classifies every refusal except a 412 stale-revision as uncertain, including definite 403, 409 and 422 problem responses. Nothing is resent, but the caller sees a definite refusal as an unknown outcome. Fix: classify the problem responses that prove no admission as refused, or record the simplification in the README.
4. (low) manager/test/service_http.py PASS pi-client line and the final step of ext-pi/test/manager-live.test.ts: the PASS line says the delivered events equal the polling listing, but the test checks only a prefix. Fix: correct the wording, or require equality of the delivered ids with the listing up to the cursor of the last delivered event.
5. (low) ext-pi/README.md, Service configuration section: it says that submit approves requests, but doc/api/README.md near 335 says that approve requires submit and control. Fix: state that approve requires submit and control.
6. (low) ext-pi/src/manager/session.ts near 622-628: waitFor ignores installed read failures, so a persistent 403 or 404 appears as TransportUnavailable only after the 120-second timeout. Fix: end the wait on a non-transient read failure and return that failure.

Non-blocking findings of fess audit fess/pe-PE9-r2.md (2026-10-01) on subtask PE9 (one admission deadline through the stacked Store locks).

1. (medium) The deadline covers one Store request, not one HTTP route (manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Commands.hs near 944, Drafts.hs near 391 and 464, Admission.hs near 270 and 920). Authentication, commandPreflight and the submission are separate requests, and each has its own five-second allowance. One answer or decision route can still wait more than the seven-second client timeout under contention. Fix: carry one deadline across the Store requests of one HTTP route, or document the route-level bound against the client timeout.
2. (medium) Inside a protected view, a route owner that reads through its own unscoped store starts a fresh gate allowance (about 29 call sites in 11 modules, for example Commands.withCommand runRead store; Authorization.hs near 136-145). A protected GET can wait up to five seconds for its first observation and up to five more for the owner read. Fix: thread the scoped store of the view into the route callbacks, or pass it through AuthorizedView.
3. (low) The deadline is wall-clock from scope entry, not from the first wait, so admitted work between waits uses it up (Store.hs near 136-142, Drafts.hs near 189-226, for example a slow readParent in createLineageDraft). Fix: state this in manager/STORAGE.md, or start the deadline at the first wait.
4. (low) The negative controls of the stacked cases failed by an uncaught StoreDeadline from the holder's own operation bound, not by a labelled FAIL line (PE/PE9/impl-r2/control-store.log, control-command.log). Fix: have the holder catch its own StoreDeadline so a regression fails on the labelled elapsed-time check.
5. (low, done in the PE9 commit) The handoff current-state text described the stacked allowances as open. The Integrator updated it.

Also disclosed by the implementer and still open: effect-first owners (capture upload, collectCaptures, changeDraftInputGuarded, export publication and completeExport, dispatch effect recording, reconcileDrafts), Configuration.withActive (unbounded withMVar), artifactResponseWait, the attempts of repeatChangedRead and the ingestion-head retry keep fresh allowances.

(medium) manager/test/ConformanceCheck.hs lines 355-358 and 380, and bisim/manager/README.md line 290: when the chosen candidate is submitted at a slot other than the chosen slot, judge returns Nothing and any non-error reply is accepted. At a held slot the model must refuse, so an oracle or model that admits the oldest eligible candidate into an occupied slot is not detected. Fix: for the chosen candidate at another slot, expect ResponseRefused when the slot is held, and otherwise ResponseAccepted with the expected admission state at that slot. Update the README table row and rerun the admission lane at seed 20261002.

This is a real conformance gap that the generator avoids and that the README records only as a limit. Fix: an owner decision on the model or the policy for a reduced capacity.
4. (low) evidence PF/PF12/impl-r1/wrong-slot-control.log: the local mismatch control exercised only the next-state path. No control showed that the lane catches an oracle that accepts a candidate that the policy does not choose. Fix (optional): run a second local control that flips the expected outcome of a non-chosen candidate to accepted, and do not commit it.

5. (low) bisim/ci/manager.sh lines 145, 151, 186, 193: the counterexample directory is created inside a command substitution in an argument, so a mktemp failure does not trip set -e and the lane receives an empty --counterexamples path. Fix: assign the directory to a local variable first.

Non-blocking findings of fess pg-PG1-r1 (fess/pg-PG1-r1.md) on subtask PG1 (capacity host-load rule and harness cleanup).

1. (low) manager/test/service_http.py, CapacityHarness.reaping: the previous SIGTERM handler (SIG_DFL) is put back before the reap loop. A second SIGTERM during the loop, which can wait up to 25 s for each process, ends the harness at once, and the managers not yet reaped stay alive. Fix: put back the handler after the reap loop, or ignore SIGTERM while the loop runs.
2. (low) manager/test/service_http.py (storage, routes and failure measure modes) and manager/CAPACITY.md: the host-load end keys are written only when the mode succeeds, so a failed mode keeps only its start keys. CAPACITY.md does not state this exception. Fix: write the end keys in a finally block, or state the exception in CAPACITY.md.
3. (low) manager/test/service_http.py per-lifetime finally blocks in route_checks, worker_failure_checks, manager_failure_checks, tui_failure_checks and storage_checks: they still send terminate and wait 25 s with no kill, and only the dispatch-level reaping() completes the cleanup, so two stop paths exist. Fix: route these blocks through CapacityHarness.reap.

Open items from the PG1 limitations: no run of record exists until the orphan processes (PIDs 61004, 111 and 9444) are ended and the one-minute load is at most 16. Frontend processes that the TUI modes start are not in the reaping list.

Findings of the Phase B part 1 end-of-part review (packages and safety lenses over 9a641dd8..2f0848b1) that no tracker item held. The handoff section "End-of-part review" in doc/workflow-manager-handoff.md states each one.

1. Medium. The download quota of one refuses a second concurrent download at once with 429 storage-quota. Only the 5-second timeout of each 16 KiB write bounds a download, so one slow client can hold a 64 MiB download for hours. Before B6 a second download waited up to five seconds. Disposition: a wait for the quota within the five-second allowance, a total deadline for one download, or an operator ruling, plus a two-client download case in WM-028.
2. Medium. GET /v1/requests and GET /v1/runs select every request and run of the authorized profiles with no row bound before paging. Disposition: a bounded id query that refuses with view-too-large before materialization, or keyset pages, with the bound in doc/api/README.md.
3. Medium. The service binds no legacy retention root, so /v1/runs lists no legacy history. WM-025 stays open until the service binds the retention roots read-only or a deferral is recorded.
4. Low. The WM-023 scope change during retained responses is shown only as an observe-only boundary.
5. Low. An event stream holds no Store reader charge for its lifetime, so only the subscription quota and globalConnections bound the number of streams.
6. Low. Held controls of a run that fails before carrying them, for a reason other than cancel, get no acknowledgement if the process exits first.
7. Low. Some assertions of the boundary and events-lifecycle modes accept two refusal codes (400 or 404, 429 or 503).

Open findings of the end-of-part review of Phase B part 2 (two lenses, range 5e8bbf9f..00686da1, both "approve with notes", no critical or high finding). The table "End-of-part review" in doc/workflow-manager-handoff.md is the source.

Medium:
1. A lost run or a command ask with no receipt reply protects its segment in every later lifetime, so the pruner floor stops and the manager log grows toward its allowance. No operation clears either case. Possible repair: answer orphaned asks at restart and treat a lost run as terminal for pruning. (Store.hs pruneCandidate, segmentProtected; Commands.hs recordReceipt)
2. After a manager crash the quarantined reservation keeps its slot and resource keys. With the default of one execution reservation, no new run starts until WM-042 adds a quarantine release. (manager/WORKERS.md, failures-manager)
3. Legacy history is not windowed. Each page of /v1/runs reads every bound root in full within 256 entries and 1 MiB, and a larger root refuses the whole collection. (History.hs legacyRuns, legacyItems)
4. A live re-route stops the attempt in the runtime, but no caller sends session/cancel to the adapter, so the stopped ACP turn stays open until that engine shuts down. (Exec.hs withPhysicalAttempt, Acp.hs cancelTurn)

Low:
5. A redirect that arrives after the attempt returned its answer drops the answer and asks the chosen candidate again. (Exec.hs withPhysicalAttempt)
6. The pruner evaluates the age trigger only at the open and after a seal. (Store.hs withManagerLogPruner)
7. The fold of an in-flight redirect without a dispatch builds a dispatch with one target, so a second live redirect of the same occurrence would fail the fold. No current path reaches it. (Snapshot.hs, ext-pi/src/reducer.ts)
8. doc/api/README.md "Pages and live delivery": the general paragraph says a page set holds one revision, and the next paragraph says each window of /requests and /runs reads its own database boundary.
9. The part 2 openapi comparison in the stage directory accepts added optional properties, and the gate list named only the route paths. The rule is not a repository check. (B2/C26/impl-r1/api_additive_v2.py)
10. The ext-pi supervisor does not originate a live redirect. The service TUI sends one through /v1 since PC23 (digit keys in the run monitor). The local TUI mode still redirects only inside the dispatch window. (ext-pi/src/supervisor.ts)
11. The functional low gaps of part 1 stay open (tracked in acat-phase-b1-review-followups-dk1v).

The closeout corrected the documentation that findings 1 to 3 name (manager/STORAGE.md, doc/api/README.md, the handoff). Findings 1 and 2 are the functional repairs that Phase C needs first.

Findings of the Phase C end-of-phase review (two lenses, range cc29f51a..cb62e35e, both "approve with notes", no critical or high finding) that no earlier tracker item holds. The section "End-of-phase review" under "Phase C of 2026-10" in doc/workflow-manager-handoff.md is the source.

1. (medium) release-quarantine releases only with terminal-record or no-launch evidence. A reservation whose run was launched and wrote no runtime terminal record (for example, the runtime died with the manager) reads cleanup-required and cannot be released. With the default executionReservations of 1, such a crash still blocks every later run. (manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Quarantine.hs, manager/WORKERS.md)
2. (medium) At 80x24 the summary review has no spare row. A restart, resume or fork review, and a review with a long profile identifier, are refused with "does not fit". The lineage path needs a resize before an approval, and tui-history approves the restart child at 100x30. (tui/src/Agentic/Tui/Presentation.hs)
3. (low) The Manager overview lists a run with lost supervision, and its request, as live, because its filters test only terminal_observed=0, while the pruner now treats such a run as terminal. After a crash and a release the lost run stays in the overview as an active run. (manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Overview.hs)
4. (low) After cancelOnStop the engine drops every session/update and refuses every permission on that connection until the reply to the cancelled prompt arrives. An adapter that never replies to a cancelled prompt would empty the answers of every later turn on that connection. ACP requires the reply. Item 1 of acat-pc7-acp-cancel-fess-3lb2 holds the repair. (engine/acp/src/Agentic/Acp.hs)

The other review findings are held by acat-70ll (unresolved approve after a restart), acat-pc17-follow-fess-jd40 (overview fence after a 410), acat-jdmd (40x12 monitor), acat-a6a7-fess-followup-1exm, acat-a10a11-fess-followup-33k1 and acat-a5s2b-fess-followup-s9rl (Phase A polish), acat-pc8-tui-polish-fess-y3yt and acat-ftw9 (retrieval retry), acat-w8t0, acat-pc14-endpoint-switch-fess-2oup and acat-w92x.

Deferred security stage for Phase E, Pi service mode (WM-036 to WM-038), under the operator direction of 2026-09-30 (functionality first, security in a later stage). acat-wm-036-5ndj, acat-wm-037-dz3v and acat-wm-038-mgb7 are met for function at closeout commit a17a015b with these items deferred. They stay open only because acat-wm-035-9uqq (WM-035), a functional dependency of WM-036, is open. The list matches section "Deferred security items" under "Phase E of 2026-10" in doc/workflow-manager-handoff.md. The Phase C and Phase B part 2 items stay in acat-phase-c-deferred-security-5eso and acat-phase-b2-deferred-security-k1hl.

- Name Constraints parity in the TypeScript client, and the per-response
  credential check of the Haskell client. The `ext-pi` client uses the
  default TLS validation of Node with the profile CA file only. This goes
  with the remaining Name Constraints work, patch B18 included.
- Credential-file hardening in TypeScript beyond the functional checks of
  private mode, owner and size: an `O_NOFOLLOW` open, a link-count check and
  descriptor reads that are safe against a change between check and use.
- Strict JSON in the TypeScript client: refusal of duplicate members and of
  deep nesting in SSE data and answers.
- Secret-marker scans that show that the bearer never appears in Pi
  transcripts, tool results, notifications, logs or crash output.
- A separate model credential, so that the manager log records a
  model-initiated action under its own principal.
- Hostile tool-argument and prompt-injection negatives for the
  `agent_cat_workflow` tool beyond the functional checks that a grant or
  approval field never grants.
- Hostile-input and transport negatives for the TypeScript client beyond
  the shared vectors: malformed SSE frames, slow streams, cross-origin
  credential forwarding and proxy environment probes.
- Revocation-during-stream matrices for `ext-pi`.
- Redaction projections of manager data in Pi transcript entries and
  widgets.
- A threat model for Pi service mode and a security gate for WM-036 to
  WM-038.
- An analysis of owner-lock spoofing for the quarantine evidence of PE3. A
  process of the same account could hold or release `owner.lock`, and an
  engine could close the inherited descriptor early.
- A review of the test hooks in shipped extension code. The stream hooks of
  PE25 register only when `AGENT_CAT_PI_TEST_HOOKS` is 1.
- The mode check of the root-role marker file in `ext-pi`.
- The G2 observation-only witness, the hostile-input and transport
  negatives of WM-024 and WM-028, and every item of the deferred security
  stage of the Phase C section below and of section 8 of the
  remaining-scope report.

Findings of the Phase F end-of-phase review (two lenses, packages and working, ranges 77b256fd..88d999b7 and emacs-native c839f75..6e8eac0, both "approve with notes", no critical or high finding). The section "Open findings" under "Phase F part 3 of 2026-10-03" in doc/workflow-manager-handoff.md is the source. The next run fixes the functional items at their owners.

1. (Medium, both lenses) Event read path under burst. Runtime ingestion, stream batch reads, the view check before each stream write and the page reads share one configuration guard and two database readers (globalDatabaseReaders). events.catch-up-p50-ms measured 1065.4 and 3253.9 ms against 1000, and events.catch-up-p95-ms 19521.6 and 27230.6 ms against 5000 (PF20, PF24). The owner decides between a separate reader budget for stream checks and ingestion and a revised ceiling with a stated reason. (manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Store.hs, the SSE route)
2. (Medium, packages lens) Interrupted backup. failures.backup.passed is false, because the case needs the restore-marker boundary of the admission_audit.py copy, and that case covers an interrupted restore. Make an interrupted-backup boundary reachable from manager-admission-check or a service_http.py mode, or obtain operator permission to run that one subcommand of admission_audit.py once. (WM-042 owns offline backup and restore.)
3. (Medium, working lens) Measurements depend on host load. The capacity-streams pass of record came from a rerun at load average 13 after a failure at 47 with no fix. pages.first-page-p50-ms measured 1716.4 and 535.6 ms against 500 at high load, and 281.1 ms in PF18. Record host load as a measurement condition in manager/CAPACITY.md, take one idle-host measurement, or revise the ceiling with a stated reason.
4. (Low) Truncated GET bodies under Store contention: the manager cuts off a non-streaming GET body or closes with no response where a 503 is expected. The harness retries. No check shows that the TUI, Emacs and Pi clients do so.
5. (Low) readDraftAt repeats while it holds the file slot: repeatChangedRead sleeps 10 ms between attempts with the slot held, up to the five-second allowance, once for each member of a collection or overview read. (manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Drafts.hs)
6. (Low) Disk write failure stops the safety path: after the first EFBIG the Store refuses every later read and command, cancel and withdraw included, until a restart. manager/CAPACITY.md (safety-path section) and manager/STORAGE.md do not state this.
7. (Low) SSE reconnection after a drop inside a batch meets 429 storage-quota more often, because the subscription stays until the next write fails. No client documents a retry bound for this 429.
8. (Low) Orphaned managers: CapacityHarness.begin does not end its manager when a step after Popen fails. PID 61004 (PF17) and the stopped PIDs 111 and 9444 (Phase E) were present at 2026-10-03T07:10Z.
9. (Low) Pin statements: the node_modules/@earendil-works/* entries of ext-pi/package-lock.json still name 0.84.3 and 0.85.1 with registry URLs, and manager/README.md still states coding-agent 0.85.1 (see acat-pf3-fess-followup-ann7).
10. (Low) Emacs witness search: service_history_open in ci/emacs-ui.py (emacs-native) passes the run id to re-search-forward without regexp-quote, and only a batch check covers a child row listed first.

The closeout review of Phase G (two lenses, both "approve with notes", no critical or high finding) left these findings that no other issue tracks. The section "Phase G of 2026-10", subsection "Open findings", of doc/workflow-manager-handoff.md states each one.

- Medium: `pages.first-page-p50-ms` measures about 400 ms in the PG26 runs against 131.2 ms in PG4 on the same `History.hs`. When the capacity runs of record run on an idle host, compare the value with 131 ms. If it stays near 400 ms, measure the first-page path between `76da0f5c` and the head before G5 is declared.
- Low: `administerLocally` runs without a handler in `recordedServing`. An exception that is not an `IOException`, `AdminFailure` or `StoreFailure` ends the linked server thread and the manager, and the command record gets no receipt.
- Low: the comment of `advanceAuthorizationRevision` in manager/src/Agentic/Manager/Store.hs says that the manager has no such change, but `reloadServing` in LocalAdmin.hs now calls it.
- Low: the status result of `LocalAdminResponse` at `88d999b7` had `additionalProperties: false`, so a strict client refuses the nine added properties. No client in the tree reads local-administration status.
- Low: PG6 and PG12 changed the import graph of manager modules without building every executable that imports them. A subtask that changes that graph builds every such executable.

The PG22 findings R1 and R4 stay in acat-pg22-review-lows-ncss, and the missing capacity runs of record stay in acat-n50o and acat-jkas.
